source: Dionysii Cartusiani Opera Omnia, t. X (Montreuil)

1.title: Elucidatio litteralis capituli primi: Onus verbi Domini ad Israel.
1.title_en: Literal explanation of the first chapter: The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel.

paras.t: Ut refert S. Hieronymus, Malachias prophetavit ad populum Juda, hoc est ad tribum Juda ac Benjamin, atque ad sacerdotes, post reditum a Babylone, post Aggæum et Zachariam. Hebræi quoque affirmant hunc Malachiam fuisse Esdram scribam ac sacerdotem : quod et Hieronymus approbare videtur, quamvis certum non sit. Magister enim in historiis scribit, quod Malachias post regressum a Babylonica captivitate, natus sit in Judæa in Sophis : quem, quia optimæ vitæ fuit, et adspectu decorus, populus appellavit Malachiam, id est angelum. Mortuus est autem, dum adhuc juvenis erat, et in agro suo sepultus. Et quia huic Prophetæ non præmittitur titulus tempus sui vaticinii exprimens, tenendum est, secundum Hieronymum, eum eodem tempore prophetasse, quo illi qui hunc Prophetam immediate præcedunt et titulum tempus prophetiæ exprimentem habent, quamvis sua vaticinatio, illorum vaticinationem secuta dicatur.
paras.en: As St. Jerome relates, Malachias prophesied to the people of Juda, that is, to the tribe of Juda and Benjamin, and to the priests, after the return from Babylon, after Aggeus and Zacharias. The Hebrews also affirm that this Malachias was Esdras the scribe and priest; and Jerome too seems to approve this, although it is not certain. For the Master in the Histories [that is, Peter Comestor, in his Historia scholastica] writes that Malachias was born in Judea, at Sophis, after the return from the Babylonian captivity; and because he was of excellent life and comely to look upon, the people called him Malachias, that is, angel. He died while still young, and was buried in his own field. And since no title is set before this Prophet stating the time of his prophecy, we must hold, according to Jerome, that he prophesied at the same time as those who immediately precede this Prophet and have a title stating the time of their prophecy, although his prophesying is said to have followed theirs.

paras.t: Titulus autem hujus Prophetæ est: Onus verbi Domini ad Israel in manu Malachiæ. Itaque, Onus verbi Domini, id est pondus increpationis, verbo prophetico ac divino significatum. Vel, ut alii dicunt, Onus verbi Domini, id est officium annuntiandi divinitus revelata. Officium enim alicui injunctum, onus ejus vocatur. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : Assumptio verbi Domini. Verumtamen, secundum Hieronymum, quandocumque in exordio Prophetarum ponitur, Onus, insinuatur quod ea quæ subsequuntur, molestiis plena sint, ita quod onus, pondus malorum significat. Hoc igitur onus verbi Domini, sanctum, et dici jussum est ad Israel, id est ad Judæos a Babylone reductos. Hi namque Israel sibi nomen retinuerunt, aliis decem tribubus, quæ Israel appellari solebant, in captivitate manentibus. Et bene ait, Ad Israel, et non, Contra Israel, quia ad eorum emendationem onus hoc ordinabatur. In manu Malachiæ, id est per subministrationem Malachiæ, vel per ipsum Malachiam : per manum enim operatio designatur, et sæpe pars pro toto accipitur. Septuaginta transtulerunt : In manu angeli ejus. Malachias namque interpretatur angelus Domini. Propter quod nonnulli dixerunt, quod Propheta hic fuit angelus in corpore humano : quod vanum, falsum, ac frivolum est. Non enim sequitur : nomen hoc, angelus Domini interpretatur, ergo vir ita vocatus, angelus fuit. Sicut non sequitur, Osee prophetam fuisse salvatorem, quanquam nomen istud Osee, interpretetur salvator; vel Joelem fuisse Deum, eo quod Joel interpretetur Deus meus.
paras.en: Now the title of this Prophet is: [[1:1|The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachi.|Onus verbi Domini ad Israel in manu Malachiæ]] And so, [[1:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]], that is, the weight of rebuke signified by the prophetic and divine word. Or, as others say, [[1:1|The burden of the word of the Lord|Onus verbi Domini]], that is, the office of announcing what has been divinely revealed: for an office laid upon someone is called his burden. Hence the Septuagint translated: The taking up of the word of the Lord. Yet, according to Jerome, whenever *Burden* is set at the opening of the Prophets, it is a hint that what follows is full of troubles, so that *burden* signifies a weight of evils. This burden of the word of the Lord, then, holy [so the print, *sanctum*; perhaps a slip for *factum*, “that came”], was also commanded to be spoken [[1:1|to Israel|ad Israel]], that is, to the Jews brought back from Babylon. For these kept the name of Israel for themselves, while the other ten tribes, which used to be called Israel, remained in captivity. And he says well, *To Israel*, and not *Against Israel*, because this burden was ordained for their amendment. [[1:1|By the hand of Malachi|In manu Malachiæ]]: that is, through the ministry of Malachias, or through Malachias himself; for by the hand an activity is meant, and often the part is taken for the whole. The Septuagint translated: By the hand of his angel. For Malachias is interpreted *angel of the Lord*. For this reason some have said that this Prophet was an angel in a human body: which is vain, false and frivolous. For it does not follow: this name is interpreted *angel of the Lord*, therefore the man so called was an angel; just as it does not follow that the prophet Osee was the saviour, although the name Osee is interpreted *saviour*; or that Joel was God, because Joel is interpreted *my God*.

paras.t: Denique Dominus ostendit onus præfatum non injuste ad Israel fieri, quia divinæ dilectioni fuerunt ingrati. Dilexi vos, dicit Dominus; et dixistis. Multa quippe pietatis suæ dona Deus specialiter Judæorum plebi exhibuit. Propter quod in Deuteronomio Moyses dixit : Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus, et amavit semen eorum post eos. Sed quomodo ingratos et reprobos fertur Deus amasse? Dicendum, quod omnia diligit quoad bonam naturam, quam habent a Creatore. Quosdam etiam reprobos dilexisse interdum asseritur, propter specialia beneficia quæ eis in vita præsenti impendit. Solos vero prædestinatos absolute et proprie diligit, etsi non subinde secundum præsentem justitiam, dum impie vivunt, tamen secundum prædestinationem æternam, qua eis finaliter misereri instituit. Ingratitudo insuper et temeritas Judæorum ostenditur ex responsione eorum ad Dominum. Quemadmodum autem Deus per Prophetam loquitur eis, sic et ipsi ad Prophetam loquendo, Deo respondent, vel immediate ad Deum dirigunt verbum, ac dicunt : In quo dilexisti nos ? id est, per quid apparet specialis dilectio tua ad nos, quos ita affligi permittis ? Non enim attenderunt quod Salomon scribit : Quem diligit Dominus, corripit. Quibus Dominus clementer respondit : Nonne frater erat Esau Jacob ? dicit Dominus. Quasi dicat, Utique : ut patet in Genesi. Et dilexi Jacob, etiam antequam eum creavi, quia non ex meritis suis ipsum elegi, sed ex mea bonitate ei benefacere decrevi, et in amore eum præveni, volens eum esse vas misericordiæ in salutem, ut in eo mea pietas reluceret.
paras.en: Next the Lord shows that the burden spoken of is not laid upon Israel unjustly, because they were ungrateful for God's love. [[1:2|I have loved you, saith the Lord: and you have said|Dilexi vos, dicit Dominus; et dixistis]]. For God showed many gifts of his kindness especially to the people of the Jews; wherefore Moses said in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 10:15|the Lord hath been closely joined to thy fathers|Patribus tuis conglutinatus est Dominus]], and loved [[Deut 10:15|their seed after them|semen eorum post eos]]. But how is God said to have loved the ungrateful and the reprobate? It must be said that he loves all things as regards the good nature which they have from the Creator. He is also sometimes said to have loved certain of the reprobate, because of the special benefits which he bestows on them in this present life. But he loves the predestined alone absolutely and properly: if not always according to present justice, while they live wickedly, yet according to the eternal predestination by which he has resolved to have mercy on them in the end. Moreover, the ingratitude and rashness of the Jews is shown by their answer to the Lord. For just as God speaks to them through the Prophet, so they too, speaking to the Prophet, answer God, or address their word directly to God, and say: [[1:2|Wherein hast thou loved us?|In quo dilexisti nos ?]] that is, by what does thy special love for us appear, when thou allowest us to be so afflicted? For they did not heed what Solomon writes: [[Prov 3:12|whom the Lord loveth, he chastiseth|Quem diligit Dominus, corripit]]. To them the Lord answered mercifully: [[1:2|Was not Esau brother to Jacob, saith the Lord|Nonne frater erat Esau Jacob ? dicit Dominus]]? As if to say: Certainly, as is plain in Genesis[[Gen 25:25||]]. [[1:2|And I have loved Jacob|Et dilexi Jacob]], even before I created him; for I did not choose him for his merits, but resolved of my goodness to do him good, and went before him in love, willing him to be a vessel of mercy unto salvation, so that my kindness might shine forth in him.

paras.t: Esau autem odio habui, id est, juste reliqui, et propter ejus demerita, quæ præscivi, reprobandum duxi. Dedit etiam Deus benedictionem paternam, et hereditatis promissionem ipsi Jacob, non Esau, quum tamen Esau primogenitus esset. Porro peccata Esau in Genesi describuntur : qualiter voluit fratrem suum Jacob occidere, et pro lenticula primogenita vendidit. Unde de ipso dicit ad Hebræos Apostolus, quod non invenit pœnitentiæ locum, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam. Etenim illa ejus pœnitentia ex qua flevit, non fuit pœnitentia vera et virtuosa, ex divino amore et zelo justitiæ odioque peccati procedens, sed ex dolore amissionis rei terrenæ, vel ex servili timore. Præterea locum istum, Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui, allegat et tractat Apostolus ad Romanos, ad ostendendum quod prædestinatio, electio, et gratia Dei, non sunt ex operibus nostris seu meritis. Ait namque : Quum nondum nati fuissent, aut aliquid egissent boni aut mali (ut secundum electionem propositum Dei maneret), non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, dictum est : Quia major serviet minori, sicut scriptum est : Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui.
paras.en: [[1:3|But have hated Esau|Esau autem odio habui]], that is, I justly left him, and for his demerits, which I foreknew, resolved to reprobate him. God also gave the father's blessing and the promise of the inheritance to Jacob himself, not to Esau, though Esau was the firstborn[[Gen 27:1||]]. Moreover, the sins of Esau are described in Genesis: how he wished to kill his brother Jacob[[Gen 27:41||]], and sold his birthright for a little lentil pottage[[Gen 25:29||]]. Hence the Apostle says of him to the Hebrews that he [[Heb 12:17|found no place of repentance, although with tears he had sought it|non invenit pœnitentiæ locum, quanquam cum lacrimis inquisisset eam]]. For that repentance of his, out of which he wept, was not a true and virtuous repentance, proceeding from the love of God, zeal for justice and hatred of sin, but from grief at the loss of an earthly thing, or from servile fear. Further, the Apostle cites and treats this passage, [[1:2|I have loved Jacob|Jacob dilexi]], [[1:3|But have hated Esau|Esau autem odio habui]], in the Epistle to the Romans, to show that predestination, election and the grace of God are not from our works or merits. For he says: [[Rom 9:11|when the children were not yet born, nor had done any good or evil (that the purpose of God according to election might stand)|Quum nondum nati fuissent, aut aliquid egissent boni aut mali (ut secundum electionem propositum Dei maneret]], [[Rom 9:12|Not of works, but of him that calleth, it was said|non ex operibus, sed ex vocante, dictum est]]: [[Rom 9:12|The elder shall serve the younger|Quia major serviet minori]], [[Rom 9:13|As it is written: Jacob I have loved: but Esau I have hated|sicut scriptum est : Jacob dilexi, Esau autem odio habui]].

paras.t: Insuper quod Deus Esau habuerit odio, consequenter ostenditur per hoc, quod posteros quoque ejus reliquerit. Et posui montes ejus in solitudinem, id est, habitacula filiorum Esau in montibus sita, redegi per Nabuchodonosor regem Babylonis in loca deserta habitatore carentia; et hereditatem ejus, id est terras et urbes ac villas eorum, quas hereditarie possidebant, in dracones deserti, id est, in tantum vastavi et demolitus sum per regem præfatum, ut dracones et cetera bruta quæ in desertis solent morari, habitarent ibidem. Quod si dixerit Idumæa, id est gens Idumææ de semine Esau orta, Destructi sumus, id est, habitacula nostra destructa, et multi de plebe nostra occisi sunt, sed revertentes ad propriam terram, ædificabimus quæ destructa sunt; hæc dicit Dominus exercituum : Isti Idumæi ædificabunt, et ego destruam, id est, opus eorum non prosperabitur ; et vocabuntur hi Idumæi, termini impietatis, id est terra impietatibus plena. Terra enim pro populo eam inhabitante, et populus pro terra habitationis suæ accipi solet, et unum per aliud designari. Et populus cui iratus est Dominus usque in æternum, id est, Idumæi isti dicentur populus a Deo perpetue derelictus. De hac autem Idumææ pressura, dictum est supra in visione Abdiæ prophetæ : de qua etiam vastitate in Isaia et Jeremia plura leguntur. Et oculi vestri videbunt, id est, dejectionem istam Idumææ, o Judæi, agnoscetis, vel corporaliter adspicietis ; et vos dicetis : Magnificetur Dominus super terram Israel, id est, terram nostram Judææ dignetur Deus magnifice reparare atque protegere, ne nobis contingat ut Idumæis.
paras.en: Moreover, that God held Esau in hatred is next shown by his having forsaken his posterity also. [[1:3|and I have made his mountains a wilderness|Et posui montes ejus in solitudinem]]: that is, the dwellings of the sons of Esau, set in the mountains, I reduced through Nabuchodonosor king of Babylon to desert places without inhabitant; [[1:3|and given his inheritance|et hereditatem ejus]], that is, their lands, cities and villages, which they possessed by inheritance, [[1:3|to the dragons of the desert|in dracones deserti]], that is, I laid them waste and destroyed them so far, through the aforesaid king, that dragons and the other beasts that are wont to dwell in deserts lived there. [[1:4|But if Edom shall say|Quod si dixerit Idumæa]], that is, the nation of Idumea sprung from the seed of Esau, [[1:4|We are destroyed|Destructi sumus]], that is, our dwellings are destroyed and many of our people slain, [[1:4|but we will return|sed revertentes]] to our own land [[1:4|and build up what hath been destroyed|ædificabimus quæ destructa sunt]]: [[1:4|thus saith the Lord of hosts|hæc dicit Dominus exercituum]]: [[1:4|They shall build up, and I will throw down|Isti Idumæi ædificabunt, et ego destruam]], that is, their work shall not prosper; [[1:4|and they shall be called|et vocabuntur]], these Idumeans, [[1:4|the borders of wickedness|termini impietatis]], that is, a land full of wickedness. For the land is commonly taken for the people dwelling in it, and the people for the land they dwell in, and the one is signified by the other. [[1:4|and the people with whom the Lord is angry for ever|Et populus cui iratus est Dominus usque in æternum]]: that is, these Idumeans shall be called a people forsaken by God for ever. Of this oppression of Idumea it was said above, in the vision of Abdias the prophet [that is, in Denis's commentary on Abdias]; and of this devastation too much is read in Isaias[[Is 34:1||]] and Jeremias[[Jer 49:7||]]. [[1:5|And your eyes shall see|Et oculi vestri videbunt]], that is, you shall recognise this overthrow of Idumea, O Jews, or behold it with your bodily eyes; [[1:5|and you shall say: The Lord be magnified upon the border of Israel|et vos dicetis : Magnificetur Dominus super terram Israel]] [the text has *terram*, “land”; the margin gives the other reading *terminum*, “border”, as in the Douay-Rheims], that is, may God deign to restore our land of Judea magnificently and protect it, lest it befall us as it befell the Idumeans.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus arguit populum Judæorum, quod eum nec honorabant ut patrem, nec metuebant ut Dominum. Et aliqui dicunt, quod sermo sequens specialiter dirigatur ad sacerdotes ; sed Hieronymus asserit, quod loquitur eis qui sub Zorobabel et Jesu filio Josedec et Esdra ac Nehemia de Babylonia sunt reversi, constructoque altari, nondum ædificaverunt templum, nec muros Jerusalem, et nihilo minus in peccatis pristinis permanebant, Deum nec amore, nec timore venerantes. Itaque ait : Filius honorat patrem. Hoc enim est primum præceptum secundæ tabulæ, in qua erant septem præcepta ad proximum pertinentia. Et filii boni hoc faciunt patribus tam carnalibus quam spiritualibus, sicut Apostolus docet et jubet ad Ephesios : Filii, obedite patribus vestris in Domino. Et servus dominum suum, supplendum est, timet. Est autem duplex timor, puta servilis, quo pœna, non culpa, timetur; et filialis, quo culpa metuitur. Simili modo duplex est servitus. Servus ergo servitute timoris pure servilis, non meretur dici filius Dei, nec est in statu salutis, quia caritatem non habet. Unde hujusmodi servum Christus distinguens a filio Dei adoptivo, ait : Servus non manet in domo in æternum, filius autem manet in æternum; et alibi, Servus nescit quid faciat Dominus ejus. Porro servus servitute timoris casti ac filialis, etiam filius est : de quo dicit Salvator, Euge, serve bone et fidelis, intra in gaudium Domini tui. Quum autem jam inter filium et servum fiat distinctio, videtur nunc sermo fieri de timore servili, qui licet non faciat bonum bene et meritorie, scilicet recta intentione et caritative, retrahit tamen a peccato, estque initium sapientiæ, quia disponit ad gratiam. Unde scriptum est : Timor Domini expellit peccatum. Et iterum ait Scriptura : Per timorem Domini declinat unusquisque a malo.
paras.en: Next the Lord rebukes the people of the Jews because they neither honoured him as a father nor feared him as a Lord. Some say that the discourse that follows is addressed especially to the priests; but Jerome asserts that he is speaking to those who came back from Babylon under Zorobabel and Jesus the son of Josedec, and Esdras and Nehemias, and who, having built the altar, had not yet built the temple or the walls of Jerusalem, and none the less went on in their former sins, worshipping God neither with love nor with fear[[1 Esd 3:1||]][[1 Esd 9:1||]][[2 Esd 13:1||]]. And so he says: [[1:6|The son honoureth the father|Filius honorat patrem]]. For this is the first commandment of the second table, which held the seven commandments concerning our neighbour. And good sons do this to their fathers, carnal and spiritual alike, as the Apostle teaches and commands to the Ephesians: [[Eph 6:1|Children, obey your parents in the Lord|Filii, obedite patribus vestris in Domino]] [Denis reads *patribus*, “fathers”, for *parentibus*, “parents”]. [[1:6|And the servant his master|Et servus dominum suum]]: understand *fears*. Now fear is twofold: servile, by which punishment, not guilt, is feared; and filial, by which guilt is feared. In like manner servitude is twofold. The servant, then, in the servitude of purely servile fear does not deserve to be called a son of God, nor is he in the state of salvation, because he has not charity. Hence Christ, distinguishing such a servant from the adopted son of God, says: [[John 8:35|the servant abideth not in the house for ever: but the son abideth for ever|Servus non manet in domo in æternum, filius autem manet in æternum]]; and elsewhere: [[John 15:15|the servant knoweth not what his lord doth|Servus nescit quid faciat Dominus ejus]]. But the servant in the servitude of chaste and filial fear is also a son: of whom the Saviour says, [[Matt 25:21|Well done, good and faithful servant|Euge, serve bone et fidelis]], [[Matt 25:21|enter thou into the joy of thy lord|intra in gaudium Domini tui]][[Matt 25:23||]]. Since a distinction is here already made between the son and the servant, the word seems now to be of servile fear, which, though it does not do good well and meritoriously (that is, with a right intention and out of charity), yet draws one back from sin, and is [[Ecclus 1:16|the beginning of wisdom|initium sapientiæ]], because it disposes to grace. Hence it is written: [[Ecclus 1:27|The fear of the Lord driveth out sin|Timor Domini expellit peccatum]]. And again Scripture says: [[Prov 15:27|by the fear of the Lord every one declineth from evil|Per timorem Domini declinat unusquisque a malo]].

paras.t: Si ergo pater ego sum, id est, quum sim pater vester per creationem, legislationem, atque multiplicis beneficii collationem, et si digne vereque me patrem vocatis (juxta illud Isaiæ : Tu, Domine, pater noster, redemptor noster), ubi est honor meus? id est, cur præceptis meis non obeditis, nec actibus latriæ me honoratis, orando, laudando, gratias referendo, sacrificando, et omne opus Dei reverenter implendo? Maledictus enim qui facit opus Dei negligenter. Et si Dominus ego sum, sicut utique sum, et specialiter Dominus vester per providentiam singularem. Denique solus Deus est Dominus per universalem præsidentiam, propriam auctoritatem, atque fontalem legum, præceptorum ac jurium lationem; omnesque alii dominatores comparantur ad ipsum sicut ministri et instrumenta ad dominum ac principalem agentem. Hinc ait per Isaiam : Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum, et gloriam meam alteri non dabo. Ubi est timor meus, id est mihi impendendus? Qualiter autem isti Judæi multum negligentes fuerunt in opere Dei, patet ex præinductis super Aggæum et Zachariam.
paras.en: [[1:6|If then I be a father|Si ergo pater ego sum]]: that is, since I am your father by creation, by the giving of the law, and by bestowing benefits of many kinds, and if you worthily and truly call me father (according to that of Isaias: [[Is 63:16|thou, O Lord, art our father, our redeemer|Tu, Domine, pater noster, redemptor noster]]), [[1:6|where is my honour?|ubi est honor meus?]] that is, why do you not obey my commandments, nor honour me with acts of latria [that is, the worship owed to God alone], by praying, praising, giving thanks, sacrificing and fulfilling every work of God with reverence? For [[Jer 48:10|Cursed be he that doth the work of the Lord deceitfully|Maledictus enim qui facit opus Dei negligenter]] [Jer 48:10, not noted in the margin; Denis reads “negligently”, *negligenter*, where the Vulgate has “deceitfully”, *fraudulenter*]. [[1:6|And if I be a master|Et si Dominus ego sum]], as I certainly am, and your Lord especially by a singular providence. For God alone is Lord by universal rule, by authority of his own, and as the fountain from which laws, commandments and rights are given; and all other rulers are compared to him as ministers and instruments to their lord and principal agent. Hence he says by Isaias: [[Is 42:8|I the Lord, this is my name: I will not give my glory to another|Ego Dominus, hoc est nomen meum, et gloriam meam alteri non dabo]] [the margin gives Is. xliii, 8; the words are Is 42:8]. [[1:6|where is my fear|Ubi est timor meus]], that is, the fear owed to me? How very negligent these Jews were in the work of God is plain from what was brought forward on Aggeus and Zacharias.

paras.t: Deinde sacerdotes specialiter arguuntur. Ad vos, o sacerdotes, loquor, qui despicitis nomen meum, id est, majestatem meam in sacrificando et immolando non honoratis, nec mihi paretis; et dixistis, impudenter respondendo ac scisitando (sicut et Cain, qui dixit: Numquid custos fratris mei sum ego?): In quo despeximus nomen tuum?
paras.en: Then the priests in particular are rebuked [the words that follow end v. 6 in the Vulgate; the Douay-Rheims sets them at the start of v. 7]. [[1:7|To you, O priests|Ad vos, o sacerdotes]], I speak, [[1:7|that despise my name|qui despicitis nomen meum]], that is, who do not honour my majesty in sacrificing and offering victims, nor obey me; [[1:7|and have said|et dixistis]], answering and questioning shamelessly (as Cain too did, who said: [[Gen 4:9|am I my brother's keeper?|Numquid custos fratris mei sum ego?]]): [[1:7|Wherein have we despised thy name?|In quo despeximus nomen tuum?]]

paras.t: Quibus Deus respondet: Offertis super altare meum pollutum panem, id est panes propositionis non tales quales offerre tenemini. Sacerdotes quippe, secundum Hebraicam traditionem, panes propositionis propriis manibus pistare, formare, et coquere debuerunt, ut dicit Hieronymus: quod isti neglexerunt, sumentes quoscumque de medio. Et dicitis, negligentiam vestram dissimulando: In quo polluimus te, id est, te et sacramenta tua violavimus, seu irreverenter tractavimus? Quemadmodum autem dicimur Deum sanctificare, dum ei in sanctitate atque justitia ministramus, sicque quantum in nobis est, eum esse sanctum monstramus; sic dicimur eum polluere, dum irreverentialiter et vitiose nos coram ipso, præsertim in suo cultu, habemus, atque per hoc, quantum in nobis est, eum quasi non sanctum ac inhonorandum esse ostendimus. In eo quod dicitis, Mensa Domini despecta est, id est per hoc quod affirmatis altare templi non oportere honorari in sacrificiis legis et panibus propositionis ut olim, quia nondum honorifice reparatum est vel ornatum, sed quasi vile et indecorum. Putabant enim sic posse subtrahi altari de sanctimonia religionis, sicut defuit ei de gloria ædificii primi altaris a Salomone constructi.
paras.en: God answers them: [[1:7|You offer polluted bread upon my altar|Offertis super altare meum pollutum panem]], that is, loaves of proposition not such as you are bound to offer. For according to the Hebrew tradition, as Jerome says, the priests were to knead, shape and bake the loaves of proposition with their own hands; and these neglected it, taking any loaves at all from the common stock. [[1:7|And you say|Et dicitis]], hiding your negligence: [[1:7|Wherein have we polluted thee?|In quo polluimus te]] that is, how have we violated thee and thy sacraments, or handled them irreverently? Now just as we are said to sanctify God when we minister to him in holiness and justice, and so, as far as in us lies, show him to be holy, so we are said to pollute him when we behave irreverently and viciously before him, above all in his worship, and by this, as far as in us lies, show him to be as it were not holy and not to be honoured. [[1:7|In that you say: The table of the Lord is contemptible|In eo quod dicitis, Mensa Domini despecta est]]: that is, in that you assert that the altar of the temple ought not to be honoured with the sacrifices of the law and the loaves of proposition as of old, because it has not yet been honourably restored or adorned, but is as it were mean and unseemly. For they thought that the altar could thus be deprived of the holiness of religion, just as it fell short of the glory of the building of the first altar, built by Solomon.

paras.t: Si offeratis cæcum ad immolandum, id est, si animal cæcum adducatis, ut Domino immoletur, nonne malum est? id est, imo hoc illicitum est, et lege prohibitum. Et si offeratis Domino claudum vel languidum animal, nonne malum est? Hoc enim per Moysen Deus prohibuit. Quod autem hoc malum sit, Dominus probat per locum a minori. Offer illud duci tuo, id est, si domino tuo mortali terreno, qui est vermis et pulvis, tale animal offerres, si placuerit ei, id est, non placebit, aut si susceperit faciem tuam, id est, præsentiam tuam non habebit gratam, dicit Dominus exercituum. Multo minus Deo omnipotenti talis placebit oblatio.
paras.en: [[1:8|If you offer the blind for sacrifice|Si offeratis cæcum ad immolandum]], that is, if you bring a blind animal to be sacrificed to the Lord, [[1:8|is it not evil?|nonne malum est?]] that is, nay, this is unlawful and forbidden by the law[[Deut 15:21||]]. [[1:8|And if you offer the lame and the sick|Et si offeratis Domino claudum vel languidum animal]], [[1:8|is it not evil?|nonne malum est?]] For God forbade this through Moses[[Deut 15:21||]]. That this is evil the Lord proves by an argument from the lesser. [[1:8|Offer it to thy prince|Offer illud duci tuo]]: that is, if thou wert to offer such an animal to thy mortal earthly lord, who is a worm and dust, [[1:8|if he will be pleased with it|si placuerit ei]], that is, he will not be pleased; [[1:8|or if he will regard thy face|aut si susceperit faciem tuam]], that is, he will not welcome thy presence, [[1:8|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]]. Much less will such an offering please Almighty God.

paras.t: Deinceps post increpationem ad pœnitentiam eos invitat. Et nunc deprecamini vultum Dei, id est divinæ pietatis respectum, ut misereatur vestri (de manu enim vestra factum est hoc, id est, præscriptum peccatum vos commisistis, offerentes Deo animalia lege prohibita), si quo modo suscipiat facies vestras, id est, si forte aliquo modo vobis indulgere dignetur. Loquitur autem conditionaliter, non quod dubitet Deum vere pœnitentibus paratum ignoscere, sed quia certum non est an pœnitentia nostra sit vera et Deo accepta, quippe quum nec nos esse in caritate noscamus. Vel ideo ait, Si, ut pensemus peccata enormia non qualemcumque, sed dignam ac proportionatam exigere contritionem ut deleantur. Siquidem magnitudini culpæ æquari debet pœnitentiæ magnitudo, secundum Hieronymum.
paras.en: Then, after the rebuke, he invites them to penance. [[1:9|And now beseech ye the face of God|Et nunc deprecamini vultum Dei]], that is, the regard of the divine kindness, [[1:9|that he may have mercy on you|ut misereatur vestri]] ([[1:9|for by your hand hath this been done|de manu enim vestra factum est hoc]], that is, you have committed the sin described above, offering to God animals forbidden by the law), [[1:9|if by any means he will receive your faces|si quo modo suscipiat facies vestras]], that is, if perhaps he will deign in some way to pardon you. He speaks conditionally, not because he doubts that God is ready to forgive those who truly repent, but because it is not certain whether our repentance is true and acceptable to God, since we do not even know that we are in charity[[Eccles 9:1||]]. Or he says *if* so that we may consider that enormous sins require, if they are to be blotted out, not just any contrition, but one worthy of them and proportioned to them. For the greatness of the penance ought to equal the greatness of the guilt, according to Jerome.

paras.t: Quis est in vobis, qui claudat ostia et incendat altare meum gratuito? id est, nullus ministrorum templi deservit mihi in templo sine mercede, quum nec janitores claudant januas templi, nec alii supponant ignem altari ad holocausta cremanda sine emolumento, seu vitæ stipendio: habebant enim decimas omnium frugum quæ offerebantur a populo: idcirco peccata vestra graviora sunt, pœnitentiamque majorem requirunt. Ex quo, secundum Hieronymum, ostenditur acceptiorem Deo esse servitutem quæ in præsenti mercedem non postulat. Propter quod Apostolus gratis Evangelium prædicavit, et manuum labore victum accepit, ne quemquam gravaret.
paras.en: [[1:10|Who is there among you, that will shut the doors, and will kindle the fire on my altar gratis?|Quis est in vobis, qui claudat ostia et incendat altare meum gratuito?]] that is, none of the ministers of the temple serves me in the temple without wages, since neither do the doorkeepers shut the gates of the temple, nor do others put fire to the altar for burning the holocausts, without payment or a living; for they had the tithes of all the fruits that were offered by the people. Therefore your sins are the graver, and require a greater penance. From this, according to Jerome, it is shown that the service which asks no reward in the present life is more acceptable to God. For this reason the Apostle preached the Gospel freely[[2 Cor 11:7||]], and got his living by the labour of his hands, so as to be burdensome to no one[[2 Cor 11:9||]][[1 Thess 2:9||]][[2 Thess 3:8||]].

paras.t: Vituperata Judæorum oblatione, ostenditur sacrificium Deo gratissimum. Non est mihi voluntas in vobis, id est, mihi vita vestra non placet, nec vos, dicit Dominus exercituum; et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra, id est, sacrificia vestra jam dicta, et eis similia, non acceptabo propter vestra facinora. Sacrificia nempe veteris Testamenti non habuerunt virtutem et acceptabilitatem ex parte operis operati, videlicet rei oblatæ, sed operis operantis, puta ex devotione et gratia offerentis. Verumtamen istud referendum est maxime ad tempus novi Testamenti, in quo veteris legis sacrificia cessaverunt, et carnalibus victimis spirituales hostiæ successerunt. Ideo subditur : Ab ortu enim solis usque ad occasum, id est ubique terrarum, magnum est nomen meum in gentibus, id est, excellentia majestatis meæ cunctis populis innotescit : sicut Isaias prædixit, Repleta est terra scientia Domini. Istud enim factum est per Apostolorum prædicationem, quibus jussit Salvator : Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ. Et in omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda, id est Eucharistiæ sacramentum, omnium legalium sacrificiorum finis et veritas. Propterea, ejus oblatione publicata, cessaverunt mortifera, quæ fuerunt sacrificia illa legalia. Quia magnum est nomen meum in gentibus, scilicet tempore evangelicæ legis : juxta illud : Domine, Dominus noster, quam admirabile est nomen tuum in universa terra !
paras.en: Having found fault with the offering of the Jews, he shows the sacrifice most pleasing to God. [[1:10|I have no pleasure in you|Non est mihi voluntas in vobis]], that is, your life does not please me, nor do you, [[1:10|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]]; [[1:10|and I will not receive a gift of your hand|et munus non suscipiam de manu vestra]], that is, your sacrifices just spoken of, and others like them, I will not accept, because of your crimes. For the sacrifices of the Old Testament did not have their power and acceptableness on the part of the work wrought, that is, of the thing offered, but on the part of the one working, namely from the devotion and grace of the one offering [that is, *ex opere operato* and *ex opere operantis*: they availed not by the rite performed but by the dispositions of the offerer]. Yet this is to be referred above all to the time of the New Testament, in which the sacrifices of the old law ceased, and spiritual offerings took the place of carnal victims. Therefore he adds: [[1:11|For from the rising of the sun even to the going down|Ab ortu enim solis usque ad occasum]], that is, everywhere on earth, [[1:11|my name is great among the Gentiles|magnum est nomen meum in gentibus]], that is, the excellence of my majesty becomes known to all peoples: as Isaias foretold, [[Is 11:9|the earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord|Repleta est terra scientia Domini]]. For this was done through the preaching of the Apostles, whom the Saviour commanded: [[Mark 16:15|Go ye into the whole world and preach the gospel to every creature|Euntes in mundum universum, prædicate Evangelium omni creaturæ]]. [[1:11|and in every place there is sacrifice, and there is offered to my name a clean oblation|Et in omni loco sacrificatur et offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]], that is, the sacrament of the Eucharist, the end and the truth of all the sacrifices of the law. Therefore, once its offering was made known, those sacrifices of the law ceased, which had become deadly [that is, after the Gospel was proclaimed, to keep the old rites was itself a sin]. [[1:11|for my name is great among the Gentiles|Quia magnum est nomen meum in gentibus]], namely in the time of the law of the Gospel; according to that saying: [[Ps 8:2|O Lord, our Lord, how admirable is thy name in the whole earth!|Domine, Dominus noster, quam admirabile est nomen tuum in universa terra]]

paras.t: Et vos, o Judæi, polluistis illud, id est, inhonorastis me, in eo quod dicitis : Mensa Domini contaminata est. Hoc jam paulo ante dictum est atque expositum. Hic enim accipitur mensa pro altari, quia subjungitur : et quod superponitur, contemptibile est cum igne qui illud devorat. Ignis enim non devoravit panes propositionis, sed carnes in altari oblatas. Eadem enim ratione nunc dicunt mensam Domini contaminatam, qua supra dixerunt eam despectam, quia videlicet altare nondum ornatum aut pretiose constructum fuit. Ideo putabant ipsum non oportere ut olim honorari, nec sacrificia de perfectis, sanis, et integris animalibus fieri. Simili ratione ignem qui in altari nutriebatur ad holocausta cremanda, contemptibilem reputabant.
paras.en: [[1:12|And you|Et vos]], O Jews, [[1:12|have profaned it|polluistis illud]], that is, have dishonoured me, [[1:12|in that you say: The table of the Lord is defiled|in eo quod dicitis : Mensa Domini contaminata est]]. This was said and explained a little before[[1:7||]]. For here *table* is taken for the altar, since there follows: [[1:12|and that which is laid thereupon is contemptible with the fire that devoureth it|et quod superponitur, contemptibile est cum igne qui illud devorat]]. For the fire did not devour the loaves of proposition, but the flesh offered on the altar. For they now call the table of the Lord defiled for the same reason for which they called it contemptible above, namely because the altar was not yet adorned or richly built. Therefore they thought that it need not be honoured as of old, nor sacrifices made of perfect, sound and whole animals. For a like reason they reckoned contemptible the fire that was kept up on the altar for burning the holocausts.

paras.t: Et dixistis vos excusando : Ecce de labore, id est, hoc ipsum quod offerimus, de labore nostro est, vel cum difficultate obtulimus, eo quod nuper de Babylone reversi, pauperes simus, et exsufflastis illud, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, oblationem vestram exsufflatione mea dignam fecistis, et virtutem ac meritum ejus vestra inobedientia exstinxistis; et intulistis in templum, de rapinis claudum et languidum, id est animalia claudicantia, et infirma per rapinam adepta, et intulistis munus, id est, talia immolastis. Numquid suscipiam illud de manu vestra? dicit Dominus exercituum. Non utique, quum ibi sit duplex transgressio, puta rapina, quæ est contra proximum, et prævaricatio legis divinæ talia offerri vetantis, quæ est iniquitas contra Deum.
paras.en: [[1:13|And you have said|Et dixistis]], excusing yourselves: [[1:13|Behold of our labour|Ecce de labore]]: that is, this very thing that we offer is of our labour, or we have offered it with difficulty, because, having lately returned from Babylon, we are poor; [[1:13|and you puffed it away, saith the Lord of hosts|et exsufflastis illud, dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, you have made your offering worthy of being puffed away by me [that is, blown away in contempt], and by your disobedience have quenched its virtue and merit; [[1:13|and you brought in|et intulistis]] into the temple [[1:13|of rapine the lame, and the sick|de rapinis claudum et languidum]], that is, limping and infirm animals gotten by robbery, [[1:13|and brought in an offering|et intulistis munus]], that is, you sacrificed such things. [[1:13|shall I accept it at your hands, saith the Lord|Numquid suscipiam illud de manu vestra? dicit Dominus exercituum]]? Not at all, since there is a double transgression there: robbery, which is against one's neighbour, and the violation of the divine law that forbids such things to be offered, which is iniquity against God.

paras.t: Maledictus dolosus, qui habet in grege suo masculum, id est animal bonum et aptum ad offerendum, et votum faciens de sacrificio offerendo, immolat debile Domino, id est animal vile, claudum, cæcum, ac languidum; quia rex magnus ego, dicit Dominus exercituum. Quemadmodum enim solus Deus est Dominus per universalem providentiam et propriam auctoritatem, sic et ipse solus est rex, et rex adeo magnus, ut magnitudinis seu dignitatis et perfectionis ejus nullus sit finis. Et nomen meum horribile, id est metuendum, in gentibus quæ me vere cognoscunt : illæ enim me formidandum agnoscunt atque formidant. In ceteris quoque Deus horribilis est, per districtam et æquissimam ultionem. Quum ergo tantæ sublimitatis sit Deus, non est ei de vilioribus, sed melioribus, secundum quod ipse jussit, facienda oblatio. Hinc ad Abel et ad munera ejus respexit Deus, quia de melioribus (scilicet primogenitis) gregis sui adipibusque eorum obtulit Domino. Ad Cain vero et munera ejus non respexit, quia de fructibus terræ obtulit viliora, ut legitur in Genesi.
paras.en: [[1:14|Cursed is the deceitful man that hath in his flock a male|Maledictus dolosus, qui habet in grege suo masculum]], that is, an animal good and fit to be offered, [[1:14|and making a vow|et votum faciens]] to offer a sacrifice, [[1:14|offereth in sacrifice that which is feeble to the Lord|immolat debile Domino]], that is, a mean animal, lame, blind and sick; [[1:14|for I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts|quia rex magnus ego, dicit Dominus exercituum]]. For just as God alone is Lord by universal providence and authority of his own, so he alone is King, and a King so great[[Ps 94:3||]] that of his greatness, or dignity and perfection, there is no end[[Ps 144:3||]]. [[1:14|And my name is dreadful|Et nomen meum horribile]], that is, to be feared, [[1:14|among the Gentiles|in gentibus]] who truly know me: for they know me to be dreaded, and they dread me. In the rest too God is dreadful, by strict and most just vengeance. Since then God is of such sublimity, the offering to be made to him is not of the meaner things but of the better, as he himself commanded. Hence God had respect to Abel and to his offerings, because he offered to the Lord of the better (namely the firstlings) of his flock and of their fat[[Gen 4:4||]]; but to Cain and his offerings he had no respect, because he offered meaner things of the fruits of the earth, as is read in Genesis[[Gen 4:5||]].

paras.t: Onus verbi Domini ad Israel in manu Malachiæ. Per Malachiam, qui angelus Domini interpretatur, spiritualiter intelligitur Christus magni consilii Angelus, vel quilibet ejus sacerdos, prædicator, vel doctor, qui angelus, id est nuntius Dei est. Per hos factum est et fit verbum Dei Patris atque totius superbenedictæ Trinitatis, ad Israel, id est Ecclesiam Christi.
paras.en: [[1:1|The burden of the word of the Lord to Israel by the hand of Malachi|Onus verbi Domini ad Israel in manu Malachiæ]]. By Malachias, which is interpreted *angel of the Lord*, is spiritually understood Christ, the Angel of great counsel[[Is 9:6||]] [the margin gives Is. ix, 6, "according to the Septuagint", which names the Child *Angel of great counsel*, where the Vulgate has *Wonderful, Counsellor*], or any priest, preacher or doctor of his, who is an angel, that is, a messenger of God. By these the word of God the Father and of the whole superblessed Trinity has come and comes [[1:1|to Israel|ad Israel]], that is, to the Church of Christ.

paras.t: Dilexi vos, o Christiani, o Judæi ad Christum conversi, et omnes per Christum salvati, dicit Dominus. Hoc enim ait Christus Apostolis : Ipse Pater amat vos. Et rursus in Evangelio legitur Joannis : Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret. Et Paulus ad Ephesios : Propter nimiam, inquit, caritatem qua dilexit nos Pater, Filium suum misit in mundum. Et dixistis : In quo dilexisti nos præ ceteris gentibus? Hoc interdum fideles quasi admirando inquirunt, dum gravissimis adversitatibus atteruntur. Boni quoque inquirunt hoc, non ex ingratitudine, sed ut de ratione et modo divinæ ad eos dilectionis plenius instruantur. Mali vero ea temeritate id quærunt, qua cetera Christi beneficia aspernantur. Dominus autem respondit :
paras.en: [[1:2|I have loved you|Dilexi vos]], O Christians, O Jews converted to Christ, and all who are saved through Christ, [[1:2|saith the Lord|dicit Dominus]]. For this is what Christ says to the Apostles: [[John 16:27|the Father himself loveth you|Ipse Pater amat vos]]. And again we read in the Gospel of John: [[John 3:16|God so loved the world, as to give his only begotten Son|Sic Deus dilexit mundum, ut Filium suum unigenitum daret]]. And Paul to the Ephesians: [[Eph 2:4|For his exceeding charity|Propter nimiam]], he says, [[Eph 2:4|wherewith he loved us|caritatem qua dilexit nos]], the Father sent his Son into the world [the words "the Father sent his Son into the world" are not in Eph. ii, 4; compare Gal 4:4 and 1 John 4:9]. [[1:2|and you have said: Wherein hast thou loved us|Et dixistis : In quo dilexisti nos]] more than the other nations? The faithful sometimes ask this as if in wonder, when they are worn down by the heaviest adversities. The good ask it too, not out of ingratitude, but so as to be more fully instructed about the reason and manner of God's love for them. But the wicked ask it with the same rashness with which they spurn the other benefits of Christ. And the Lord answered:

paras.t: Nonne frater erat Esau Jacob? Per Jacob, qui interpretatur luctator vel supplantator, eratque vir quietus et simplex, in tabernaculis habitans, intelliguntur Christifideles, qui contra mundum, carnem, diabolum victoriose luctantur, et vitia vincunt. Per Esau autem, qui erat venator, et interpretatur quercus, quod est nomen arboris cibum porcorum portantis, intelliguntur carnales, concupiscentiarum sectatores, sæculares et vani. Et isti sunt fratres, quoniam boni ac mali ex eisdem protoplastis progeniti sunt. Verumtamen illos diligit, hos odit Deus; nec illi istis meliores essent, nisi a Deo præ istis æternaliter dilecti atque electi sine omni merito suo fuissent. Siquidem Deus omnipotens, justus, pius, ac sapiens, cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat; et ejus prædestinatio, totius virtutis et gratiæ in nobis est causa.
paras.en: [[1:2|Was not Esau brother to Jacob?|Nonne frater erat Esau Jacob?]] By Jacob, which is interpreted *wrestler* or *supplanter*, and who was a quiet and plain man, dwelling in tents, are understood the faithful of Christ, who wrestle victoriously against the world, the flesh and the devil, and overcome vices. But by Esau, who was a hunter, and whose name is interpreted *oak*, which is the name of a tree that bears the food of swine, are understood the carnal, the followers of their lusts, the worldly and vain. And these are brothers, since the good and the wicked were begotten of the same first parents. Yet God loves the former and hates the latter; nor would the former be better than the latter, had they not been loved and chosen by God from eternity before the latter, without any merit of their own. For God, almighty, just, merciful and wise, [[Rom 9:18|hath mercy on whom he will. And whom he will, he hardeneth|cujus vult miseretur, et quem vult indurat]]; and his predestination is the cause of all the virtue and grace in us.

paras.t: Et posui montes ejus, scilicet Esau, in solitudinem. Montes Esau, sunt potentes et magni in sæculo isto, qui ad dignitates et dominationes adspirant : qui in solitudinem rediguntur, quia ut scriptum est : Omnis potentatus brevis est vita; sic et rex hodie est, et cras morietur. In primo quoque libro Machabæorum dicitur : A verbis peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus, stercus et vermis ; hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur. Et hereditatem ejus, id est corpora eorum quæ diligenter colunt et nutriunt, posui in dracones deserti, id est, in putredinem pulveremque redegi : juxta illud Ecclesiastici, Quum morietur homo, hereditabit serpentes et bestias et vermes. Vel in dracones deserti ponentur, quando in inferno dæmonibus in tormentis sociabuntur, juxta illud Judith : Deus omnipotens dabit ignem et vermes in carnem ipsorum, ut urantur et sentiant usque in sempiternum.
paras.en: [[1:3|and I have made his mountains|Et posui montes ejus]], that is, Esau's, [[1:3|a wilderness|in solitudinem]]. The mountains of Esau are the mighty and great in this world, who aspire to dignities and lordships: they are brought to a wilderness, because, as it is written: [[Ecclus 10:11|All power is of short life|Omnis potentatus brevis est vita]]; [[Ecclus 10:12|so also a king is to day, and to morrow he shall die|sic et rex hodie est, et cras morietur]]. In the first book of the Machabees too it is said: [[1 Mach 2:62|fear not the words of a sinful man, for his glory is dung and worms|A verbis peccatoris ne timueritis, quia gloria ejus, stercus et vermis]]; [[1 Mach 2:63|Today he is lifted up, and tomorrow he shall not be found|hodie extollitur, et cras non invenietur]]. [[1:3|and given his inheritance|Et hereditatem ejus]], that is, their bodies, which they carefully tend and feed, I have given [[1:3|to the dragons of the desert|in dracones deserti]], that is, I have brought them to rottenness and dust: according to that saying of Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 10:13|when a man shall die, he shall inherit serpents, and beasts, and worms|Quum morietur homo, hereditabit serpentes et bestias et vermes]]. Or they will be given to the dragons of the desert when in hell they are made companions of the demons in torments, according to that saying of Judith: [[Jdt 16:20|the Lord almighty|Deus omnipotens]] [[Jdt 16:21|will give fire, and worms into their flesh, that they may burn, and may feel for ever|dabit ignem et vermes in carnem ipsorum, ut urantur et sentiant usque in sempiternum]].

paras.t: Quod si dixerit Idumæa, id est plebs ista terrena per Esau designata, Destructi sumus, id est humiliati, et plagati a Deo, qui cornua animositatum nostrarum confregit, sed revertentes ad pristina mala, ædificabimus quæ destructa sunt, scilicet turrim superbiæ, vana consilia, et pompositates mundanas ; hæc dicit Dominus : Isti ædificabunt, et ego destruam. Deus enim superbis resistit ; et sedes ducum superborum destruxit. Et vocabuntur homines isti Deo adversantes, termini impietatis, et populus cui iratus est Dominus usque in æternum. Sunt enim terreni impietatibus pleni, qui æterna oblivione relinquentur a Deo. Quibus dicit Jacobus : Agite nunc, divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis vestris : thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus. De quibus loquitur Jeremias : Domine, omnes qui te derelinquunt, confundentur; recedentes a te, in terra scribentur.
paras.en: [[1:4|But if Edom shall say|Quod si dixerit Idumæa]], that is, this earthly people signified by Esau, [[1:4|We are destroyed|Destructi sumus]], that is, humbled and struck by God, who has broken the horns of our high spirits, [[1:4|but we will return|sed revertentes]] to our former evils, [[1:4|and build up what hath been destroyed|ædificabimus quæ destructa sunt]], namely the tower of pride, vain counsels and worldly pomps; [[1:4|thus saith the Lord|hæc dicit Dominus]]: [[1:4|They shall build up, and I will throw down|Isti ædificabunt, et ego destruam]]. For [[1 Pet 5:5|God resisteth the proud|Deus superbis resistit]]; and [[Ecclus 10:17|hath overturned the thrones of proud princes|sedes ducum superborum destruxit]]. And these men who set themselves against God [[1:4|shall be called|vocabuntur]] [[1:4|the borders of wickedness, and the people with whom the Lord is angry for ever|termini impietatis, et populus cui iratus est Dominus usque in æternum]]. For they are earthly men full of wickedness, who will be left by God in everlasting forgetfulness. To them James says: [[Jas 5:1|Go to now, ye rich men: weep and howl in your miseries|Agite nunc, divites, plorate ululantes in miseriis vestris]]: [[Jas 5:3|You have stored up to yourselves wrath against the last days|thesaurizastis vobis iram in novissimis diebus]]. Of them Jeremias speaks: [[Jer 17:13|O Lord|Domine]], [[Jer 17:13|all that forsake thee shall be confounded: they that depart from thee, shall be written in the earth|omnes qui te derelinquunt, confundentur; recedentes a te, in terra scribentur]].

paras.t: Et oculi vestri, id est mentes, o veri Christiani, videbunt impiorum damnationem, et dicetis : Magnificetur Dominus super terram Israel, id est, gratiose ac clementissime faciat suæ Ecclesiæ, ipsum fideliter intuenti. Impiorum enim punitio bonos provocat ad meliora, juxta illud Proverbiorum : Impio flagellato, sapiens sapientior erit. Ideo, felix quem faciunt aliena damna peritum.
paras.en: [[1:5|And your eyes|Et oculi vestri]], that is, your minds, O true Christians, [[1:5|shall see|videbunt]] the damnation of the wicked, [[1:5|and you shall say: The Lord be magnified upon the border of Israel|et dicetis : Magnificetur Dominus super terram Israel]] [Denis reads *terram*, "the land", where the Vulgate has *terminum*, "the border"], that is, may he deal graciously and most mercifully with his Church, which looks faithfully to him. For the punishment of the wicked spurs the good on to better things, according to that saying of Proverbs: [[Prov 19:25|The wicked man being scourged|Impio flagellato]], the wise man shall be wiser [Denis reads *sapiens*, "the wise man", where the Vulgate has *stultus*, "the fool"]. Therefore, happy is he whom the losses of others make wise [a proverbial verse, not Scripture].

paras.t: Filius honorat patrem, etc. Quum Dominus noster Jesus Christus nos ita orare docuerit, Pater noster qui es in cœlis, sanctificetur nomen tuum : vigilantissime perpendendum est nobis, ne tam ineffabili Dei omnipotentis dignationi inveniamur ingrati; sed filiali amore Deum præ omnibus diligamus, et per sanctam caritatem affectuosissime jugiter honoremus, præsertim quum per Christum simus præcipue ad Dei filiationem vocati. Quotquot enim receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri. Nempe quum Filius Dei factus est frater noster, nos quoque filii Dei facti sumus. Non itaque indigne Deum patrem vocemus, ne nobis objiciat : Si pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus? Præterea, væ eis qui Deum nec venerantur ut patrem, nec verentur ut Dominum.
paras.en: [[1:6|The son honoureth the father|Filius honorat patrem]], etc. Since our Lord Jesus Christ has taught us to pray thus: [[Matt 6:9|Our Father who art in heaven, hallowed be thy name|Pater noster qui es in cœlis, sanctificetur nomen tuum]], we must consider most watchfully that we be not found ungrateful for so unspeakable a condescension of almighty God; but let us love God above all things with a son's love, and through holy charity honour him continually with the deepest affection, especially since through Christ we have been called above all to be sons of God. For [[John 1:12|as many as received him, he gave them power to be made the sons of God|Quotquot enim receperunt eum, dedit eis potestatem filios Dei fieri]]. Indeed, since the Son of God became our brother, we too have been made sons of God. Let us not, then, call God father unworthily, lest he cast up at us: [[1:6|if then I be a father, where is my honour?|Si pater ego sum, ubi est honor meus?]] Moreover, woe to those who neither revere God as a father nor fear him as Lord.

paras.t: Ad vos, o sacerdotes Ecclesiæ, qui despicitis nomen meum, corpus meum et sanguinem irreverenter tractando, indevote sumendo, qui carnaliter turpiterque vivendo, maximam mihi irreverentiam facitis, et alios graviter scandalizatis, dicit Dominus Jesus Christus; et dixistis : In quo despeximus nomen tuum? Quia videlicet offertis super altare meum pollutum panem, id est, sacramentum Eucharistiæ, quantum in vobis est, contaminatis, sicut et nomen Christi polluistis. Et dicitis : In quo polluimus te? id est, in quo te, o Christe, inhonoravimus? In eo quod dicitis : Mensa Domini despecta est, id est per hoc quod opere demonstratis altare esse despectum, atque a vobis esse dehonoratum, dum ad id imparati acceditis, vitiosam vitam non deserentes, neque fructuose quotidie confitentes.
paras.en: [[1:7|To you, O priests|Ad vos, o sacerdotes]] of the Church, [[1:7|that despise my name|qui despicitis nomen meum]] by handling my body and blood irreverently and receiving them without devotion, who by living carnally and shamefully show me the greatest irreverence and gravely scandalize others, says the Lord Jesus Christ; [[1:7|and have said: Wherein have we despised thy name?|et dixistis : In quo despeximus nomen tuum?]] Because, that is, [[1:7|You offer polluted bread upon my altar|offertis super altare meum pollutum panem]], that is, you defile the sacrament of the Eucharist, as far as in you lies, just as you have also polluted the name of Christ. [[1:7|and you say: Wherein have we polluted thee?|Et dicitis : In quo polluimus te?]] that is, wherein have we dishonoured thee, O Christ? [[1:7|In that you say: The table of the Lord is contemptible|In eo quod dicitis : Mensa Domini despecta est]], that is, by showing in deed that the altar is despised and dishonoured by you, when you come to it unprepared, not leaving your sinful life, nor confessing fruitfully every day.

paras.t: Si offeratis cæcum vel claudum, nonne malum est? Cæcum immolat, qui Deo obsequium indiscretum impendit. Quocontra dicit Apostolus : Rationabile obsequium vestrum. Claudum offert, qui mente nutante, et intentione non pura ac simplici, Deo precem effundit. Propter quod Jacobus apostolus ait : Vir duplex animo, inconstans est in omnibus viis suis. Languidum immolat, cujus cor in gratia Dei stabilitum non est, neque per ancoram spei firmatum in Christo. Denique verbum istud contra eos profertur, qui quum divites sint, tamen viliora et minima offerunt Creatori, modicasque eleemosynas largiuntur. Contra istos ignavos, ingratos et cupidos loquitur Deus : Offer illud duci tuo, etc., id est, si taliter homini mortali præsidenti vobis serviretis, vel supplicaretis, aut immolaretis, non ei placeret : et tamen audetis coram me vos ita habere. Hoc verbo redarguuntur negligentissimi, qui orationes, Horas et laudes Deo sine timore, attentione, reverentia et affectu exsolvunt; sed alicui magno viro, prælato aut principi locuturi aut servituri, cum reverentia magna accedunt, prudenter et distincte loquuntur, atque attoniti sunt. Nonne hi præferunt creaturam Creatori, hominem Deo, servumque Domino, et Domino tam excelso prorsus immenso?
paras.en: [[1:8|If you offer the blind|Si offeratis cæcum]] or [[1:8|the lame|claudum]], [[1:8|is it not evil?|nonne malum est?]] He offers the blind in sacrifice who renders God an indiscreet service [that is, one without discernment or right judgement]. Against this the Apostle speaks of [[Rom 12:1|your reasonable service|Rationabile obsequium vestrum]]. He offers the lame who pours out his prayer to God with a wavering mind and an intention that is not pure and single. Hence the apostle James says: [[Jas 1:8|A double minded man is inconstant in all his ways.|Vir duplex animo inconstans est in omnibus viis suis.]] He offers the sick in sacrifice whose heart is not established in the grace of God[[Heb 13:9||]], nor made firm in Christ by the anchor of hope. Lastly, this word is spoken against those who, though they are rich, yet offer the Creator the cheapest and least of things, and give small alms. Against these slothful, ungrateful and covetous men God says: [[1:8|offer it to thy prince|Offer illud duci tuo]], etc.; that is, if you served, or entreated, or offered sacrifice in this way to a mortal man set over you, it would not please him: and yet you dare to behave so before me. By this word are rebuked the most negligent, who pay God their prayers, Hours and praises without fear, attention, reverence or affection; but when they are about to speak to or serve some great man, a prelate or a prince, they come with great reverence, speak prudently and distinctly, and are struck with awe. Do not these prefer the creature to the Creator, a man to God, a servant to the Lord, and to a Lord so exalted and utterly boundless?

paras.t: Istis consulitur, imo præcipitur : Et nunc deprecamini vultum Dei, ut misereatur vestri, et emendetis vos integre.
paras.en: These are counselled, indeed commanded: [[1:9|And now beseech ye the face of God, that he may have mercy on you|Et nunc deprecamini vultum Dei, ut misereatur vestri]], and amend yourselves wholly.

paras.t: Quis est in vobis, o ministri Ecclesiæ, qui claudat ostia ecclesiæ, et incendat altare meum gratuito luminaria accendendo? quasi dicat Salvator, Nullus. Omnes enim ecclesiastici de Christi patrimonio vivunt, ideo ei reverentialius servire tenentur. Quod quum ita sit, quid fiet de his qui multa beneficia habent, aut unum superabundans, et nihilo minus vitiis pleni sunt, mundani atque carnales? quorum damnatio gravissima erit.
paras.en: [[1:10|Who is there among you|Quis est in vobis]], O ministers of the Church, [[1:10|that will shut the doors|qui claudat ostia]] of the church, [[1:10|and will kindle the fire on my altar gratis|et incendat altare meum gratuito]] by lighting the lamps? As if the Saviour said: No one. For all churchmen live on Christ's patrimony, and so they are bound to serve him the more reverently. This being so, what will become of those who hold many benefices [that is, Church offices endowed with an income], or one that is over-rich, and are nonetheless full of vices, worldly and carnal? Their damnation will be most grievous.

paras.t: In omni loco offertur nomini meo oblatio munda. Per oblationem istam intelligi potest devota oratio, juxta illud in Psalmo: Dirigatur oratio mea sicut incensum in conspectu tuo. Vel oblatio munda est, qua ipsi præcipue religiosi Deo se offerunt in holocaustum, ejus se cultui totaliter mancipantes.
paras.en: [[1:11|in every place|In omni loco]] [[1:11|there is offered to my name a clean oblation|offertur nomini meo oblatio munda]]. By this oblation may be understood devout prayer, according to that saying in the Psalm: [[Ps 140:2|Let my prayer be directed as incense in thy sight|Dirigatur oratio mea sicut incensum in conspectu tuo]]. Or the clean oblation is that by which religious especially offer themselves to God as a holocaust, giving themselves over wholly to his worship.

paras.t: Consequenter contra tenaces et irreverentes oblatores Dominus ait : Et dixistis, Ecce de labore est quod obtulimus, id est de nostra exiguitate, et nostro acquisitum sudore : ideo fecistis id dignum abjectione. Et intulistis de rapinis, id est, de bonis injuste aut violenter adeptis atque receptis, oblationem mihi fecistis. Numquid suscipiam illud de manu vestra? dicit Dominus. Quasi dicat, Nequaquam. Unde in Ecclesiastico scriptum est : Immolantis ex iniquo, iniqua est oblatio; et qui offert substantiam pauperis, quasi qui immolet filium in conspectu patris.
paras.en: Next, against stingy and irreverent offerers the Lord says: [[1:13|And you have said: Behold of our labour|Et dixistis, Ecce de labore]] is what we have offered, that is, of our scantiness, and gained by our own sweat: and so you have made it worthy to be cast away [compare the verse's *exsufflastis*, "you puffed it away"]. [[1:13|and you brought in of rapine|Et intulistis de rapinis]], that is, you have made me an offering of goods gained or received unjustly or by violence. [[1:13|shall I accept it at your hands|Numquid suscipiam illud de manu vestra?]] says the Lord. As if he said: By no means. Hence it is written in Ecclesiasticus: [[Ecclus 34:21|The offering of him that sacrificeth of a thing wrongfully gotten, is stained|Immolantis ex iniquo, iniqua est oblatio]] [Denis reads *iniqua*, "unjust", where the Vulgate has *maculata*, "stained"]; and [[Ecclus 34:24|He that offereth sacrifice of the goods of the poor, is as one that sacrificeth the son in the presence of his father|qui offert substantiam pauperis, quasi qui immolet filium in conspectu patris]].

paras.t: Maledictus dolosus, qui habet in grege suo masculum, et votum faciens, immolat debile. Hoc contra omnes intelligi potest qui quod Deo voverunt, integre non persolvunt. Quod si ita sit, quam maledicti sunt illi qui quod Deo voverunt, nec in toto, nec partim persolvunt? Et potissime hac maledictione cæduntur, qui ea voverunt quæ immediate Dei honorem et cultum concernunt, ut sunt actus virtutum. Ideo Moyses ait in Deuteronomio : Quod semel egressum est de labiis tuis, observabis, et facies sicut promisisti Domino Deo tuo. Imo nec differendum est, quum Salomon dicat in Ecclesiaste : Si quid voluisti Deo, ne moreris reddere. Et qui ita non agit, Deo fidelitatem non servat, sed maximam ei irreverentiam exhibet. Postremo, quum quid Deo de rebus nostris, actibus, aut nos ipsos offerimus, cum omni promptitudine atque lætitia mentis id faciamus : attendentes quod primo libro Paralipomenon David fatetur : Tua, Domine, sunt omnia, et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi ; unde et ego in simplicitate cordis mei lætus omnia obtuli.
paras.en: [[1:14|Cursed is the deceitful man that hath in his flock a male, and making a vow offereth in sacrifice that which is feeble|Maledictus dolosus, qui habet in grege suo masculum, et votum faciens, immolat debile]]. This can be understood against all who do not pay in full what they have vowed to God. And if that is so, how accursed are those who pay what they have vowed to God neither in whole nor in part? And those are struck by this curse most of all who have vowed things that bear directly on the honour and worship of God, such as acts of the virtues. Therefore Moses says in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 23:23|that which is once gone out of thy lips, thou shalt observe, and shalt do as thou hast promised to the Lord thy God|Quod semel egressum est de labiis tuis, observabis, et facies sicut promisisti Domino Deo tuo]]. Nay, it must not even be put off, since Solomon says in Ecclesiastes: [[Eccles 5:3|If thou hast vowed any thing to God, defer not to pay it|Si quid voluisti Deo, ne moreris reddere]]. And he who does not act so keeps no faith with God, but shows him the greatest irreverence. Lastly, when we offer God anything of our goods or our acts, or ourselves, let us do it with all readiness and gladness of mind: bearing in mind what David confesses in the first book of Paralipomenon: [[1 Par 29:14|all things are thine|Tua, Domine, sunt omnia]] [Denis adds *Domine*, "O Lord"]: [[1 Par 29:14|and we have given thee what we received of thy hand|et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi]]; [[1 Par 29:17|wherefore I also in the simplicity of my heart, have joyfully offered|unde et ego in simplicitate cordis mei lætus omnia obtuli]] [Denis adds *omnia* here and leaves out *hæc*].

2.title: Explanatio litteralis capituli secundi: Et nunc ad vos mandatum hoc, o sacerdotes.
2.title_en: Literal explanation of the second chapter: And now, O ye priests, this commandment is to you.

paras.t: Consequenter Dominus hortatur sacerdotes ad pœnitentiam, adjiciendo minas, ut qui se amore boni et zelo æquitatis non corrigunt, timore supplicii corrigantur. Et nunc ad vos mandatum hoc de observatione cultus divini in cæremoniis templi, o sacerdotes, dirigitur. Sacerdotibus quippe correctis, ceteri facilius emendantur. Si nolueritis audire auribus mentis et corporis, et si nolueritis ponere super cor, id est diligenter advertere, recolere et implere quod jubeo, ut detis gloriam nomini meo, id est, debitam mihi reverentiam impendatis, et coram aliis me clarificetis, gloriosum annuntietis, et omne mihi bonum adscribatis, ait Dominus exercituum; mittam in vos egestatem, id est terræ sterilitatem, victualiumque inopiam: quam carnales cupidique Judæi plurimum abhorrebant, præsertim quum in Deuteronomio Moyses scripserit, Omnino indigens et mendicus non erit inter vos; et maledicam benedictionibus vestris, id est fructibus terræ et ceteris bonis terrenis, quæ mea benedictione habetis, quibus et vos benedicere consuevistis, et maledicam illis, auferendo a vobis hæc dona, et opposita mala super vos inducendo; quoniam non posuistis super cor, id est, præcepta mea non impressistis memoriæ, nec debite custodistis. Quocontra dicit Psalmographus: In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi. Et Salomon ait: Serva mandata et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui. Liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam.
paras.en: Next the Lord exhorts the priests to penance, adding threats, so that those who do not amend themselves out of love of the good and zeal for equity may be amended by fear of punishment. [[2:1|And now|Et nunc]] [[2:1|this commandment|mandatum hoc]], concerning the observance of divine worship in the ceremonies of the temple, is directed [[2:1|to you|ad vos]], [[2:1|O ye priests|o sacerdotes]]. For once the priests are corrected, the rest are more easily amended. [[2:2|If you will not hear|Si nolueritis audire]] with the ears of mind and body, [[2:2|and if you will not lay it to heart|et si nolueritis ponere super cor]], that is, diligently attend to, call to mind and fulfil what I command, [[2:2|to give glory to my name|ut detis gloriam nomini meo]], that is, pay me the reverence due to me, glorify me before others, proclaim me glorious, and ascribe every good to me, [[2:2|saith the Lord of hosts|ait Dominus exercituum]]: [[2:2|I will send poverty upon you|mittam in vos egestatem]], that is, barrenness of the land and want of victuals: which the carnal and covetous Jews greatly abhorred, especially since Moses had written in Deuteronomy: [[Deut 15:4|there shall be no poor nor beggar among you|Omnino indigens et mendicus non erit inter vos]]; [[2:2|and will curse your blessings|et maledicam benedictionibus vestris]], that is, the fruits of the earth and the other earthly goods which you have by my blessing, and with which you too were wont to bless, [[2:2|yea I will curse them|et maledicam illis]], by taking these gifts away from you and bringing the opposite evils upon you; [[2:2|because you have not laid it to heart|quoniam non posuistis super cor]], that is, you have not impressed my precepts on your memory, nor kept them as you ought. Against this the Psalmist says: [[Ps 118:11|Thy words have I hidden in my heart, that I may not sin against thee|In corde meo abscondi eloquia tua, ut non peccem tibi]]. And Solomon says: [[Prov 7:2|Keep my commandments|Serva mandata]] [[Prov 7:2|and my law as the apple of thy eye|et legem quasi pupillam oculi tui]]. [[Prov 7:3|Bind it upon thy fingers, write it upon the tables of thy heart|Liga eam in digitis tuis, et in tabulis cordis tui scribe eam]].

paras.t: Ecce ego projiciam vobis brachium, id est armum animalis dextrum mihi oblatum, quia propter vestra peccata munus vestrum non habeo gratum, et dispergam super vultum vestrum stercus solennitatum vestrarum, id est, immunditiam vitiorum quæ in festis vestris committitis, et irreverentiam quam mihi facitis, in vos manifeste convertam, vos confundendo ac puniendo. Vel per stercus istud, intelligitur caro oblata continens stercora, quam Deus ob eorum peccata non acceptavit, sed eis rejecit. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt: Dispergam ventriculum, etc. Et assumet vos secum, id est, contemptibiles fœdique vitiis eritis, sicut stercus: ut tales sint offerentes, qualia ea quæ offerunt.
paras.en: [[2:3|Behold, I will cast the shoulder to you|Ecce ego projiciam vobis brachium]], that is, the right shoulder of the animal offered to me, because on account of your sins I do not hold your gift acceptable; [[2:3|and will scatter upon your face the dung of your solemnities|et dispergam super vultum vestrum stercus solennitatum vestrarum]], that is, the uncleanness of the vices which you commit on your feasts, and the irreverence which you show me, I will openly turn back upon you, confounding and punishing you. Or by this dung is understood the flesh offered with the dung still in it, which God did not accept because of their sins, but threw back at them. Hence the Septuagint translated: I will scatter the paunch, etc. [[2:3|and it shall take you away with it|Et assumet vos secum]], that is, you will be contemptible and foul with vices, like dung: so that the offerers are such as the things they offer.

paras.t: Et scietis, per justitiæ meæ effectum experientiamque vindictæ, quia misi ad vos mandatum istud, jam dictum, ut esset pactum meum, id est testamentum vel fœdus de modo sacrificiorum, cum Levi, id est Levitis ad cultum Dei specialiter dedicatis: quos etiam Deus jussit præ aliis, maculis mentis corporisque carere, et virtutum ornatu fulgere, juxta illud Exodi, Sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos; dicit Dominus exercituum.
paras.en: [[2:4|And you shall know|Et scietis]], by the effect of my justice and the experience of my vengeance, [[2:4|that I sent you this commandment|quia misi ad vos mandatum istud]] already spoken of, [[2:4|that my covenant might be|ut esset pactum meum]], that is, the testament or compact concerning the manner of the sacrifices, [[2:4|with Levi|cum Levi]], that is, with the Levites, specially dedicated to the worship of God: whom God also commanded, above others, to be free of the stains of mind and body and to shine with the adornment of the virtues, according to that of Exodus: [[Ex 19:22|The priests also that come to the Lord, let them be sanctified, lest he strike them|Sacerdotes qui accedunt ad Dominum, sanctificentur, ne percutiat eos]]; [[2:4|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]].

paras.t: Pactum meum fuit cum eo vitæ et pacis, id est, pactum vitæ et pacis percussi et inii cum tribu Levitica in deserto, eligens illam ad sacerdotium, et promittens eidem, quod si ipsa ac populus legem meam servarent, in pace viverent super terram, imo pacem pectoris et vitam gratiæ obtinerent. Porro, ut hic ait Hieronymus, quidquid nunc de Levi asseritur, ad sacerdotes et potissime ad pontifices legis Moysis pertinet. Et dedi ei timorem meum, non servilem dumtaxat, sed filialem et castum, et timuit me, et a facie nominis mei, id est consideratione majestatis meæ, pavebat. Istud in Moyse, Aaron, Eleazaro, Phinees, multisque aliis de tribu Levi exortis fuit impletum, imo et in patriarcha Levi, qui etsi interdum peccavit, postea tamen virtuosæ fuisse creditur vitæ.
paras.en: [[2:5|My covenant was with him of life and peace|Pactum meum fuit cum eo vitæ et pacis]], that is, I struck and entered into a covenant of life and peace with the tribe of Levi in the desert, choosing it for the priesthood and promising it that, if it and the people kept my law, they would live in peace upon the land, nay more, would obtain peace of heart and the life of grace. Moreover, as Jerome says here, whatever is now asserted of Levi belongs to the priests, and above all to the high priests, of the law of Moses. [[2:5|and I gave him fear|Et dedi ei timorem]] of me, not servile fear only, but filial and chaste fear [chaste fear: the fear of a loving son, who dreads to offend, as against servile fear, which dreads punishment], [[2:5|and he feared me|et timuit me]], and [[2:5|before my name|et a facie nominis mei]], that is, at the thought of my majesty, [[2:5|he was afraid|pavebat]]. This was fulfilled in Moses, Aaron, Eleazar, Phinees, and many others sprung from the tribe of Levi, nay, in the patriarch Levi too, who, though he sinned at times, is nevertheless believed to have led a virtuous life afterwards.

paras.t: Lex veritatis, scilicet lex divinitus data per Moysen, fuit in ore ejus, id est filiorum Levi, de quibus nunc dictum est, qui populum instruxerunt; et iniquitas non est inventa in labiis ejus: non quod isti ab omni iniquitate immunes exstiterint, sed quia condigne pœnituerint, et gratiam sanctitatis sortiti sint: sicut de se ipso fatetur Apostolus, Nihil mihi conscius sum; qui tamen alias loquitur, Venit Jesus peccatores salvos facere, quorum ego primus sum. In pace, id est mentis tranquillitate, et in æquitate, id est justa conversatione, ambulavit mecum, id est coram me et secundum beneplacitum meum mihi conjunctus per voluntatis conformitatem, et multos avertit ab iniquitate. Moyses enim et Aaron ac reliqui quidam posteri Aaron, plures de genere Israel ad pœnitentiam induxerunt, atque a vitiis variis retraxerunt.
paras.en: [[2:6|The law of truth|Lex veritatis]], namely the law given by God through Moses, [[2:6|was in his mouth|fuit in ore ejus]], that is, in the mouth of the sons of Levi of whom we have just spoken, who instructed the people; [[2:6|and iniquity was not found in his lips|et iniquitas non est inventa in labiis ejus]]: not that these men were free from all iniquity, but because they did fitting penance and obtained the grace of holiness: as the Apostle confesses of himself: [[1 Cor 4:4|I am not conscious to myself of anything|Nihil mihi conscius sum]]; who yet says elsewhere: [[1 Tim 1:15|Christ Jesus came|Venit Jesus]] [[1 Tim 1:15|to save sinners, of whom I am the chief|peccatores salvos facere, quorum ego primus sum]]. [[2:6|in peace|In pace]], that is, in tranquillity of mind, [[2:6|and in equity|et in æquitate]], that is, in an upright manner of life, [[2:6|he walked with me|ambulavit mecum]], that is, before me and according to my good pleasure, joined to me by conformity of will, [[2:6|and turned many away from iniquity|et multos avertit ab iniquitate]]. For Moses and Aaron, and some others of Aaron's descendants, led many of the race of Israel to penance and drew them back from various vices.

paras.t: Labia enim sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam: id est, ad sacerdotum officium pertinet congruo tempore doctrinam legis divinæ plebi proponere, et scientiam salutarem in aliis conservare. Ideo in pectore summi sacerdotis fuerat rationale, in quo Doctrina et Veritas ponebatur, quia sacerdos doctus esse debet, et præco veritatis divinæ. Et legem requirent subditi et vulgares, ex ore ejus. Unde dicit Apostolus ad Titum: Oportet episcopum sine crimine esse, amplectentem eum qui secundum doctrinam est, fidelem sermonem, ut potens sit exhortari in doctrina sana, et eos qui contradicunt, arguere; quia angelus, id est nuntius, Domini exercituum est. Quemadmodum enim divinus Dionysius docet, infimum ordinis superioris, et supremum ordinis inferioris, magnam habent mutuo convenientiam, et nomen unius transfertur ad aliud. Quum ergo in cœlesti hierarchia ordo angelorum sit infimus, et in ecclesiastica hierarchia ordo sacerdotum sit summus, angeli et sacerdotes in multis communicant: ita ut sacerdotes angeli nuncupentur, quoniam inter Deum et populum mediando, et ea quæ Dei sunt, hominibus nuntiando, atque spiritualem et angelicam vitam in carne ducendo, angelicum exercent officium. Ideo in Apocalypsi episcopi septem Ecclesiarum in Asia, angeli appellantur.
paras.en: [[2:7|For the lips of the priests shall keep knowledge|Labia enim sacerdotis custodiunt scientiam]]: that is, it belongs to the office of priests to set the teaching of the divine law before the people at the fitting time, and to preserve saving knowledge in others. Therefore on the breast of the high priest was the rational, in which Doctrine and Truth were placed[[Ex 28:29||]][[Ex 28:30||]] [the rational: the breastplate of judgment worn by the high priest], because the priest ought to be learned and a herald of the divine truth. [[2:7|and they shall seek the law|Et legem requirent]], namely subjects and common folk, [[2:7|at his mouth|ex ore ejus]]. Hence the Apostle says to Titus: [[Tit 1:7|a bishop must be without crime|Oportet episcopum sine crimine esse]], [[Tit 1:9|Embracing that faithful word which is according to doctrine, that he may be able to exhort in sound doctrine and to convince the gainsayers|amplectentem eum qui secundum doctrinam est, fidelem sermonem, ut potens sit exhortari in doctrina sana, et eos qui contradicunt, arguere]]; [[2:7|because he is the angel|quia angelus]], that is, the messenger, [[2:7|of the Lord of hosts|Domini exercituum est]]. For as the divine Dionysius teaches, the lowest of a higher order and the highest of a lower order have a great likeness to each other, and the name of the one is carried over to the other.
