paras.t: Ergo, id est, quia non prodest Deo servire, nec ipse vindicat mala, neque remunerat bona, nunc ex ista consideratione, beatos dicimus arrogantes: siquidem ædificati sunt, id est in omnibus mundi divitiis stabiliti, facientes impietatem, idola adorando: quæ est iniquitas maxima et negatio contra Deum omnipotentem, ut sanctus Job profitetur; et tentaverunt Deum, sine ullo timore peccando, et salvi facti sunt, id est, impuniti manserunt, et quod cupiebant, sortiti sunt.
paras.en: [[3:15|Wherefore|Ergo]], that is, because it profits nothing to serve God, and he neither punishes evil nor rewards good, now, from this consideration, [[3:15|we call the proud people happy|beatos dicimus arrogantes]]: for they [[3:15|are built up|siquidem ædificati sunt]], that is, established in all the riches of the world, [[3:15|that work wickedness|facientes impietatem]], by worshipping idols, [[Job 31:28|which is a very great iniquity, and a denial against|quæ est iniquitas maxima et negatio contra]] almighty God, as holy Job declares; [[3:15|and they have tempted God|et tentaverunt Deum]], by sinning without any fear, [[3:15|and are preserved|et salvi facti sunt]], that is, they have remained unpunished, and have obtained what they desired.

paras.t: Præterea sancti Prophetæ frequenter in persona infirmorum verba istis similia inveniuntur dixisse, ut est illud Jeremiæ: Justus quidem tu es, Domine, si disputem tecum; verumtamen justa loquar ad te: Quare via impiorum prosperatur, et bene est omnibus qui prævaricantur? Plantasti eos, et proficiunt. De quibus et in Psalmo cantatur: Quorum filii sicut novellæ plantationes; filiæ eorum compositæ, promptuaria eorum plena, eructantia ex hoc in illud. De hoc dictum est super Habacuc.
paras.en: Moreover the holy Prophets are often found to have said words like these in the person of the weak, as is that of Jeremias: [[Jer 12:1|Thou indeed, O Lord, art just, if I plead with thee, but yet I will speak what is just to thee: Why doth the way of the wicked prosper: why is it well with all them that transgress|Justus quidem tu es, Domine, si disputem tecum; verumtamen justa loquar ad te: Quare via impiorum prosperatur, et bene est omnibus qui prævaricantur?]] [[Jer 12:2|Thou hast planted them|Plantasti eos]], [[Jer 12:2|they prosper|et proficiunt]]. Of whom it is also sung in the Psalm: [[Ps 143:12|Whose sons are as new plants|Quorum filii sicut novellæ plantationes]]; [[Ps 143:12|Their daughters decked out|filiæ eorum compositæ]], [[Ps 143:13|Their storehouses full, flowing out of this into that|promptuaria eorum plena, eructantia ex hoc in illud]]. Of this it has been spoken on Habacuc[[Hab 1:3||]] [the margin reads *Cf. in Habac. I, 3. 16*: Denis's commentary on Habacuc 1].

paras.t: Tunc locuti sunt timentes Deum, unusquisque cum proximo suo. Timorati et illuminati a Deo Judæi, auditis tam impiis verbis malorum contra providentiam atque justitiam Dei, mutuo sunt locuti: quod videlicet Deus omnia juste disponit, nec aliquid inordinatum relinquit, et quos nunc paterne castigat, in futuro felicitat; quos autem nunc prosperari et quasi impune peccare permittit, in alia vita terribilius punit. Et attendit Dominus, et audivit justorum et impiorum universa verba, et facta consideravit. Et scriptus est liber monumenti coram eo, id est, ista a Deo jussa sunt ad perpetuam memoriam annotari et scribi, et in ejus scientia indelebiliter continentur, atque in libro conscientiæ scripta habentur, timentibus Deum et cogitantibus nomen ejus, id est ad consolationem et salutem eorum qui Deum verentur ac contemplantur.
paras.en: [[3:16|Then they that feared the Lord, spoke every one with his neighbour|Tunc locuti sunt timentes Deum, unusquisque cum proximo suo]]. The God-fearing Jews enlightened by God, having heard such impious words of the wicked against the providence and justice of God, spoke with one another: namely, that God disposes all things justly and leaves nothing out of order, and those whom he now chastises as a father he makes happy in the future, while those whom he now permits to prosper and to sin as though unpunished he punishes more terribly in the other life. [[3:16|and the Lord gave ear, and heard|Et attendit Dominus, et audivit]] all the words of the just and of the wicked, and considered their deeds. [[3:16|and a book of remembrance was written before him|Et scriptus est liber monumenti coram eo]], that is, these things were commanded by God to be noted and written for a perpetual memorial, and they are held indelibly in his knowledge, and are kept written in the book of conscience, [[3:16|for them that fear the Lord, and think on his name|timentibus Deum et cogitantibus nomen ejus]], that is, for the consolation and salvation of those who revere and contemplate God.

paras.t: Et erunt mihi isti electi, ait Dominus exercituum, in die qua ego facio, id est, qua inter electos reprobosque discernam, in peculium, id est populum familiarem et carum; et parcam eis tunc sicut mater parcit filio suo servienti sibi, id est obedienti. Tunc enim ab omni eruentur supplicio.
paras.en: [[3:17|And they shall be|Et erunt mihi]] these elect, [[3:17|saith the Lord of hosts, in the day that I do|ait Dominus exercituum, in die qua ego facio]], that is, on which I shall discern between the elect and the reprobate, [[3:17|my special possession|in peculium]], that is, a people of my household and dear to me; [[3:17|and I will spare them|et parcam eis]] then, as a mother [Denis reads *mater*, a mother, where the Vulgate has *vir*, a man] [[3:17|spareth his son that serveth him|parcit filio suo servienti sibi]], that is, obeys him. For then they will be rescued from all punishment.

paras.t: Et convertemini, id est, tunc vos, prædicti erroris assertores, ad considerandum vos et perversitatem calamitatemque vestram oculos vestros vertetis, et videbitis per effectum et exsecutionem justi judicii Dei, quid sit inter justum et impium, et inter servientem Deo et non servientem, id est, quantum Deus inter istos distinguat, quam diversa utrisque præmia reddat, euntibus impiis in ignem æternum, justis autem in felicitatem æternam.
paras.en: [[3:18|And you shall return|Et convertemini]], that is, then you who assert the aforesaid error will turn your eyes to consider yourselves and your perversity and calamity, [[3:18|and shall see|et videbitis]], by the effect and execution of God's just judgment, [[3:18|the difference between the just and the wicked: and between him that serveth God, and him that serveth him not|quid sit inter justum et impium, et inter servientem Deo et non servientem]], that is, how greatly God distinguishes between them, how different the rewards he renders to each, the wicked going into everlasting fire, but the just into everlasting happiness.

3.title: De spirituali intelligentia capitulorum tertii et quarti.
3.title_en: On the spiritual understanding of the third and fourth chapters.
3.note: This article treats chapters 3 and 4 together; its commentary on chapter 4 is shown under that chapter.

paras.t: TRIPLEX ponitur Christi adventus: primus, per incarnationem; secundus, per spiritualem visitationem seu per gratiæ infusionem; tertius, ad finale judicium. Quemadmodum autem Baptista fuit præco primi, et sicut Elias præcursor est tertii, sic quicumque electus a Deo prædicator, prælatus vel doctor, præcursor est adventus secundi. Hujusmodi enim frequenter misit Christus ante faciem suam, et mittit quotidie ad eos quorum corda per gratiam visitare disponit. Idcirco de quolibet tali dicere potest: Ecce mittam angelum meum, et præparabit viam ante faciem meam. Tales fuerunt omnes Apostoli et apostolici viri, qui hominum corda ad Christi inhabitationem præparaverunt ipsamque Ecclesiam reformaverunt. Et tunc statim venit Christus ad templum suum, id est ad conscientiæ domum, sive ad animam quæ sedes est sapientiæ.
paras.en: A THREEFOLD coming of Christ is set forth: the first, by the incarnation; the second, by spiritual visitation, or the infusion of grace; the third, to the final judgment. Now as the Baptist was the herald of the first, and as Elias is the forerunner of the third, so every preacher, prelate or doctor chosen by God is a forerunner of the second coming. For such men Christ has often sent before His face, and He sends them daily to those whose hearts He is disposed to visit by grace. Therefore He can say of each of them: [[3:1|Behold I send my angel|Ecce mittam angelum meum]] [angelus, "angel", also means "messenger"], [[3:1|and he shall prepare the way before my face|et præparabit viam ante faciem meam]]. Such were all the Apostles and apostolic men, who prepared the hearts of men for Christ to dwell in them, and reformed the Church itself. And then Christ [[3:1|presently|statim]] comes [[3:1|to his temple|ad templum suum]], that is, to the house of the conscience, or to the soul, which is the seat of wisdom[[Wis 7:27||]].

paras.t: Et quis poterit cogitare diem adventus ejus? Non enim certo scire valemus, quando Christus per caritatem et gratiam gratum facientem nos visitet, sine revelatione speciali. Propter quod scriptum est in Job: Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum; et si recesserit a me, non intelligam. Idcirco subjungitur: Et quis stabit ad videndum eum? Denique nemo novit Filium nisi Pater, visione comprehensiva, quoniam Deum nemo vidit unquam.
paras.en: [[3:2|And who shall be able to think of the day of his coming?|Et quis poterit cogitare diem adventus ejus?]] For we cannot know for certain, without a special revelation, when Christ visits us by charity and sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes a man pleasing to God]. Wherefore it is written in Job: [[Job 9:11|If he come to me, I shall not see him|Si venerit ad me, non videbo eum]]; [[Job 9:11|if he depart, I shall not understand|et si recesserit a me, non intelligam]]. Therefore it is added: [[3:2|and who shall stand to see him|Et quis stabit ad videndum eum]]? Indeed, [[Matt 11:27|no one knoweth the Son but the Father|nemo novit Filium nisi Pater]], by comprehensive vision [that is, a knowing that grasps its object wholly], since [[John 1:18|No man hath seen God at any time|Deum nemo vidit unquam]].

paras.t: Et purgabit filios Levi. Hoc facit Christus, dando sacerdotibus et religiosis gratiam emendationis, et per vicarios suos corrigendo perficiendoque clericos: quo facto, offerunt Deo sacrificia in justitia, sicut expositum est.
paras.en: [[3:3|and he shall purify the sons of Levi|Et purgabit filios Levi]]. Christ does this by giving priests and religious the grace of amendment, and by correcting and perfecting the clergy through His vicars: and when this is done, they [[3:3|offer sacrifices to the Lord in justice|offerunt Deo sacrificia in justitia]], as has been explained.

paras.t: Porro, quod subditur, Accedam ad vos in judicio, loquitur Christus contra omnes iniquos, quibus interim comminatur ut corrigantur.
paras.en: Further, in what follows, [[3:5|I will come to you in judgment|Accedam ad vos in judicio]], Christ speaks against all the wicked, whom He threatens in the meantime so that they may be corrected.

paras.t: Et vos, filii Jacob, non estis consumpti. Filii Jacob sunt Christiani, qui vitia supplantare tenentur, sicut et patres nostri in primitiva Ecclesia fecisse noscuntur. Sed, heu! multi nimis a diebus patrum nostrorum, recesserunt a legitimis Christi per hæreses, schismata, errores, ambitiones, et cetera spiritualia atque carnalia vitia. Verumtamen Christus non secundum peccata eorum reddidit eis, sed usque in præsens multis longanimiter parcit: qui utinam misericordiam et patientiam Dei super se intuerentur, et totis ad Creatorem suum præcordiis converterentur!
paras.en: [[3:6|and you the sons of Jacob are not consumed|Et vos, filii Jacob, non estis consumpti]]. The sons of Jacob are Christians, who are bound to supplant vices [Jacob means "supplanter"], as our fathers too in the primitive Church are known to have done. But alas! very many, from the days of our fathers, have departed from the ordinances of Christ, through heresies, schisms, errors, ambitions and the other spiritual and carnal vices. Yet Christ has not rendered to them according to their sins[[Ps 102:10||]], but to this day spares many with long-suffering: would that they looked upon the mercy and patience of God towards them, and turned to their Creator with their whole heart!

paras.t: Vos configitis me in decimis et primitiis. Hoc juxta sensum in præcedenti articulo positum Christus dicit contra eos qui debitas Ecclesiæ oblationes decimasque persolvere renuunt, nec curant illis temporalia sua communicare a quibus ipsi spiritualia bona suscipiunt. Ideo isti in penuria maledicti sunt : quoniam tam mortaliter in Deum peccando, omnium donorum gratiæ subtractionem merentur, nec habent spirituales divitias, sed vere nudi mente ac pauperes sunt coram Deo, deformes ac squalidi, tantoque miserabiliores, quanto interiorem suam penuriam minus attendunt et reputant. Porro, si isti debitas oblationes devote persolverint, aperiet eis Christus cataractas cœli, aquam sapientiæ salutaris eis influendo, effundetque eis benedictionem suam in abundantia, donis atque virtutibus corda eorum implendo.
paras.en: [[3:8|you afflict me|Vos configitis me]] [[3:8|in tithes and in firstfruits|in decimis et primitiis]]. This, in the sense given in the preceding article, Christ says against those who refuse to pay the offerings and tithes due to the Church, and do not care to share their temporal goods with those from whom they themselves receive spiritual goods. Therefore these [[3:9|are cursed with want|in penuria maledicti]]: for by sinning so mortally against God they deserve the withdrawal of all the gifts of grace, and they have no spiritual riches, but are truly naked in mind and poor before God, deformed and squalid, and the more wretched the less they heed and consider their inward want. But if they devoutly pay the offerings due, Christ will open to them [[3:10|the flood-gates of heaven|cataractas cœli]], pouring into them the water of saving wisdom, and will pour out on them His blessing in abundance, filling their hearts with gifts and virtues.

paras.t: Insuper dicit eisdem : Increpabo pro vobis devorantem, id est diabolum tentatorem, qui tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret. Istum conterit Christus sub pedibus devotorum velociter, sicut Apostolus loquitur ad Romanos. Et non corrumpet fructum terræ vestræ, id est, cordis vestri profectum; nec semen, quod est verbum Dei, tollet a mente. Nec erit sterilis vinea in agro, id est, anima in corpore, vel Ecclesia in sæculo, imo fructum operum virtuosorum producet.
paras.en: Moreover He says to them: [[3:11|I will rebuke for your sakes the devourer|Increpabo pro vobis devorantem]], that is, the devil, the tempter, who, [[1 Pet 5:8|as a roaring lion, goeth about seeking whom he may devour|tanquam leo rugiens circuit, quærens quem devoret]]. Him Christ crushes speedily under the feet of the devout, as the Apostle says to the Romans[[Rom 16:20||]]. [[3:11|and he shall not spoil the fruit of your land|Et non corrumpet fructum terræ vestræ]], that is, the progress of your heart; nor will he take from the mind the seed, which is the word of God[[Luke 8:12||]] [the margin gives Luke viii, 14; the seed that is the word of God is Luke 8:11, and the devil taking the word from the heart 8:12]. [[3:11|neither shall the vine in the field be barren|Nec erit sterilis vinea in agro]], that is, the soul in the body, or the Church in the world; rather it will bring forth the fruit of virtuous works.

paras.t: Præterea, quod Dominus ait : Invaluerunt super me verba vestra, et dixistis : Vanus est qui servit Deo; et quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus? etc., contra omnes pusillos, carnales rudesque dicitur, qui intuitu temporalium potius quam amore æternorum Deo utcumque deserviunt, et qui visis spiritualium hominum adversitatibus sæculariumque prosperitatibus, faciliter scandalizantur, et in fide providentiæ Dei nutare incipiunt, eosque beatificare quos temporaliter florere ac prosperari conspiciunt. Isti non norunt quam utile ac salubre sit in vita præsenti multipliciter tribulari, quam item periculosum in ea in corporalibus prosperari; nec pensant quam terribilis sit Deus in consiliis suis super filios hominum, et quod reprobos dimittit secundum desideria cordis eorum, ut eant in adinventionibus suis, eos autem quos singulariter amat, instanter exercet, et flagella eis assiduat. Verumtamen in horum imperfectorum persona dicit Job : Numquid contra hominem disputatio mea est, ut merito non debeam contristari? Quare ergo impii vivunt, sublevati sunt, confortatique divitiis? Semen eorum permanet coram eis, et non est virga Dei super eos. Hinc igitur in adversis lætemur, in prosperis formidemus. Nam quamvis mirabile sit judicium Dei, dum boni adversa et mali prospera in præsenti sæculo sortiuntur, mirabilius tamen Dei judicium est, dum electi et boni hic prosperantur, sicut Gregorius Boetiusque testantur.
paras.en: Further, what the Lord says, [[3:13|Your words have been unsufferable to me|Invaluerunt super me verba vestra]], and you have said: [[3:14|He laboureth in vain that serveth God|Vanus est qui servit Deo]]; [[3:14|and what profit is it that we have kept his ordinances|et quod emolumentum, quia custodivimus præcepta ejus?]]? etc., is said against all the faint-hearted, the carnal and the unlearned, who serve God after a fashion with an eye to temporal things rather than for love of eternal ones, and who, seeing the adversities of spiritual men and the prosperity of worldly men, are easily scandalized, and begin to waver in faith in the providence of God, and to call happy those whom they see flourishing and prospering in temporal things. These do not know how useful and wholesome it is to be troubled in many ways in the present life, and again how dangerous it is to prosper in it in bodily things; nor do they weigh how [[Ps 65:5|terrible|terribilis]] God is [[Ps 65:5|in his counsels over the sons of men|in consiliis suis super filios hominum]], and that He lets the reprobate go [[Ps 80:13|according to the desires of their heart|secundum desideria cordis eorum]], to walk [[Ps 80:13|in their own inventions|in adinventionibus suis]], while those whom He singularly loves He exercises without ceasing, and chastises with frequent scourges[[Ecclus 30:1||]]. Yet in the person of these imperfect ones Job says: [[Job 21:4|Is my debate against man, that I should not have just reason to be troubled?|Numquid contra hominem disputatio mea est, ut merito non debeam contristari?]] [[Job 21:7|Why then do the wicked live, are they advanced, and strengthened with riches?|Quare ergo impii vivunt, sublevati sunt, confortatique divitiis?]] [[Job 21:8|Their seed continueth before them|Semen eorum permanet coram eis]], [[Job 21:9|and the rod of God is not upon them|et non est virga Dei super eos]]. Hence, then, let us rejoice in adversity and be afraid in prosperity. For although the judgment of God is marvellous when the good have adversity and the wicked prosperity in this present world, yet the judgment of God is more marvellous when the elect and the good prosper here, as Gregory and Boethius testify.

paras.t: Tunc locuti sunt timentes Deum, unusquisque cum proximo suo. Hi dum infirmorum ac impiorum præinducta audiunt verba, dolent, et inter se conferunt, atque se invicem consolantes, dicunt quæ commemorata jam sunt contra illorum insaniam. Ideo erunt in die judicii quasi peculium Christi.
paras.en: [[3:16|Then they that feared the Lord, spoke every one with his neighbour|Tunc locuti sunt timentes Deum, unusquisque cum proximo suo]]. These, when they hear the words of the weak and the wicked set out above, grieve, and confer among themselves, and, consoling one another, say the things already recalled against the folly of those others. Therefore on the day of judgment they will be as the [[3:17|special possession|peculium]] of Christ.

4.title: Elucidatio capituli quarti: Ecce enim dies veniet succensa quasi caminus.
4.title_en: Explanation of the fourth chapter: For behold the day shall come kindled as a furnace.

paras.t: CONSEQUENTER Dominus de futuro […] generali judicio apertissime loquitur. Ecce enim dies veniet succensa quasi caminus, id est dies judicii in quo mundus stabit in igne conflagrationis, qui et faciem Judicis præcedens, durabit quousque sententia contra injustos prolata eos involvat, simulque cum eis in infernum descendet. Ideo scriptum est in Psalmo : Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus. De quibus jam subditur : et erunt omnes superbi et omnes facientes impietatem, stipula, id est similes stipulæ, ignis ardorem ferendo : non tamen corrumpentur ab igne, ut stipula; quanquam hi quos ignis ille invenerit hic vivos, sint occidendi ab ipso, etiam boni; sed jam de malis est sermo. Et inflammabit eos dies veniens, dicit Dominus exercituum, id est, ignis diei illius corpora reproborum incendet, etiam durante ipso judicio, quæ non relinquet eis radicem, id est fructificandi virtutem, et germen, id est perpetrationem vitiorum præteritorum, in quibus delectati fuerunt. Juxta quod scriptum est in Psalmo : Iter impiorum peribit. Et rursus de impio cantamus in Psalmo : Deus destruet te in finem, evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo, et radicem tuam de terra viventium. Hinc in Isaia legitur : Ecce Dominus in igne veniet reddere in indignatione furorem suum, et increpationem suam in flamma ignis. De hoc quoque Apostolus loquitur ad Thessalonicenses : Justum, inquiens, est apud Deum retribuere tribulationem his qui tribulant vos, in revelatione Domini nostri Jesu Christi de cœlo cum angelis virtutis ejus in flamma ignis, dantis vindictam his qui non obediunt Evangelio, qui pœnas dabunt in interitu æternas.
paras.en: NEXT the Lord speaks most openly of the future […] general judgment [a word is lost here; the sense suggests et, "and": "the future and general judgment"]. [[4:1|For behold the day shall come kindled as a furnace|Ecce enim dies veniet succensa quasi caminus]], that is, the day of judgment, in which the world will stand in the fire of the conflagration; and this fire, going before the face of the Judge, will last until the sentence pronounced against the unjust envelops them, and together with them it will go down into hell. Therefore it is written in the Psalm: [[Ps 96:3|A fire shall go before him, and shall burn his enemies round about.|Ignis ante ipsum præcedet, et inflammabit in circuitu inimicos ejus.]] Of these it is next added: [[4:1|and all the proud, and all that do wickedly shall be stubble|et erunt omnes superbi et omnes facientes impietatem, stipula]], that is, like stubble, in bearing the heat of the fire; yet they will not be consumed by the fire as stubble is; although those whom that fire finds alive here are to be killed by it, the good as well; but here the discourse is of the wicked. [[4:1|and the day that cometh shall set them on fire, saith the Lord of hosts|Et inflammabit eos dies veniens, dicit Dominus exercituum]], that is, the fire of that day will burn the bodies of the reprobate, even while the judgment itself is going on, [[4:1|it shall not leave them root|quæ non relinquet eis radicem]], that is, the power of bearing fruit, [[4:1|nor branch|et germen]] [germen, literally "shoot" or "sprout"], that is, the committing of the past vices in which they took delight. In keeping with which it is written in the Psalm: [[Ps 1:6|the way of the wicked shall perish|Iter impiorum peribit]]. And again we sing in the Psalm of the wicked man: [[Ps 51:7|will God destroy thee for ever: he will pluck thee out, and remove thee from thy dwelling place: and thy root out of the land of the living|Deus destruet te in finem, evellet te, et emigrabit te de tabernaculo tuo, et radicem tuam de terra viventium]]. Hence we read in Isaias: [[Is 66:15|behold the Lord will come with fire|Ecce Dominus in igne veniet]], [[Is 66:15|to render his wrath in indignation, and his rebuke with flames of fire|reddere in indignatione furorem suum, et increpationem suam in flamma ignis]]. Of this the Apostle too speaks to the Thessalonians: [[2 Thess 1:6|it is a just thing|Justum]], he says, [[2 Thess 1:6|with God to repay tribulation to them that trouble you|est apud Deum retribuere tribulationem his qui tribulant vos]], [[2 Thess 1:7|when the Lord Jesus shall be revealed from heaven with the angels of his power|in revelatione Domini nostri Jesu Christi de cœlo cum angelis virtutis ejus]] [[2 Thess 1:8|In a flame of fire, giving vengeance to them|in flamma ignis, dantis vindictam his]] [[2 Thess 1:8|who obey not the gospel|qui non obediunt Evangelio]], [[2 Thess 1:9|Who shall suffer eternal punishment in destruction|qui pœnas dabunt in interitu æternas]].

paras.t: Et orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum filiali et casto timore, quem caritas generat, non expellit, Sol justitiæ, id est Christus totius æquitatis et sanctitatis origo : qui tunc apparebit electis placido ac se[…] remunerator, de quo in libro Sapientiæ impii dicunt : Sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis. Quemadmodum enim sol iste visibilis cunctis suæ lucis capacibus radios influit, quantum in se est, ita et Christus omni menti creatæ dispositæ, radios sapientiæ, æquitatis et gratiæ copiose immittit. Propter quod ait : Ego sum lux mundi. Et sanitas, id est plena mentis corporisque felicitas, in pennis vestris, id est virtute et contemplatione vestra : quia et beatitudo animæ redundat in corpus. Vel pennæ istæ sunt ascensio et volatus electorum cum Christo ad cœlum, agilitasque ipsorum, qua tanquam scintillæ in arundineto discurrent.
paras.en: [[4:2|But unto you that fear my name|Et orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum]], with a filial and chaste fear, which charity begets and does not cast out, [[4:2|the Sun of justice shall arise|Sol justitiæ]], that is, Christ, the source of all equity and holiness: who will then appear to the elect as a gentle and se[…] rewarder [text is lost here at the change of column: the word begun as se… and perhaps more], of whom the wicked say in the book of Wisdom: [[Wis 5:6|the sun of understanding hath not risen upon us|Sol intelligentiæ non est ortus nobis]]. For as this visible sun pours its rays into all things capable of its light, as far as lies in it, so Christ too sends the rays of wisdom, equity and grace abundantly into every created mind that is disposed for them. Wherefore He says: [[John 8:12|I am the light of the world|Ego sum lux mundi]]. [[4:2|and health|Et sanitas]], that is, the full happiness of mind and body, in your [[4:2|wings|pennis]] [Denis reads in pennis vestris, "in your wings", where the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have "his wings"], that is, in your strength and contemplation: for the beatitude of the soul overflows into the body as well. Or these wings are the ascension and flight of the elect with Christ to heaven, and their agility, by which they [[Wis 3:7|shall run to and fro like sparks among the reeds|tanquam scintillæ in arundineto discurrent]].

paras.t: Egrediemini de carcere sæculi hujus ad patriam; vel, Egrediemini, considerando impiorum damnationem ad majorem vestram exhilarationem ; et salietis sicut vituli de armento, id est, inæstimabili replebimini gaudio, quod redundabit exuberanter in corpore. Unde Septuaginta transtulerunt : Sicut vituli de vinculis relaxati. Et calcabitis impios, quum fuerint cinis sub planta pedum vestrorum, id est, quum fuerint vobis tanquam pulvis plene subjecti : quod erit in die judicii, quando electi gaudebunt quod tantam infelicitatem misericorditer evaserunt. Idcirco divino amore incogitabiliter succendentur, et Deo præcordialissime regratiabuntur. Lætabitur nempe justus, quum viderit vindictam. Unde in Job habetur : Videbunt justi, et lætabuntur, et innocens subsannabit eos. In die qua ego facio, id est, ista complebo, hoc est in die judicii, dicit Dominus exercituum. Unde in Isaia Dominus contestatur : Egredientur, et videbunt cadavera virorum qui prævaricati sunt in me; et erunt usque ad satietatem visionis omni carni.
paras.en: [[4:2|you shall go forth|Egrediemini]] from the prison of this world to the fatherland; or, [[4:2|you shall go forth|Egrediemini]] in considering the damnation of the wicked, to your greater gladness; [[4:2|and shall leap like calves of the herd|et salietis sicut vituli de armento]], that is, you shall be filled with a joy beyond all reckoning, which will overflow abundantly into the body. Hence the Septuagint translated: Like calves loosed from their bonds. [[4:3|And you shall tread down the wicked when they shall be ashes under the sole of your feet|Et calcabitis impios, quum fuerint cinis sub planta pedum vestrorum]], that is, when they are wholly subject to you, like dust: which will be on the day of judgment, when the elect will rejoice that they have by mercy escaped so great an unhappiness. Therefore they will be kindled beyond all thought with divine love, and will give thanks to God from the depths of their hearts. For [[Ps 57:11|The just shall rejoice when he shall see the revenge|Lætabitur nempe justus, quum viderit vindictam]]. Hence it is said in Job: [[Job 22:19|The just shall see, and shall rejoice, and the innocent shall laugh them to scorn|Videbunt justi, et lætabuntur, et innocens subsannabit eos]]. [[4:3|in the day that I do this|In die qua ego facio]], that is, when I shall accomplish these things, that is, on the day of judgment, [[4:3|saith the Lord of hosts|dicit Dominus exercituum]]. Hence in Isaias the Lord solemnly declares: [[Is 66:24|And they shall go out, and see the carcasses of the men that have transgressed against me|Egredientur, et videbunt cadavera virorum qui prævaricati sunt in me]]; [[Is 66:24|and they shall be a loathsome sight to all flesh|et erunt usque ad satietatem visionis omni carni]] [literally "they shall be, to all flesh, unto the fill of seeing"].

paras.t: Mementote legis Moysis servi mei : id est, quum tam metuendum Dei judicium sit futurum, jam incessanter reminiscamini et servate legem Dei per Moysen datam ; quam mandavi ei in monte Horeb, id est Sinai, ubi data est Moysi lex scripta, et duæ tabulæ testamenti scriptæ digito Dei, ad omnem Israel, id est, ut eam omnibus filiis Israel observandam proponeret; præcepta, id est præcepta illa decem moralia, puta Decalogum legis : quæ etiam in novo Testamento jubentur servari, Christo dicente, Si vis ad vitam intrare, serva mandata; et judicia, id est præcepta judicialia, quæ determinabant modum juste vivendi ad proximum, sicut cæremonialia legis præcepta determinabant modum se habendi in cultu divino ad Creatorem. Judicialia autem legis præcepta possunt servari in novo Testamento, si ab aliquo præsidente christiano ad hoc idoneo, de novo instituantur : non enim fuerunt figurativa dumtaxat. De triplicibus autem præceptis legis, videlicet moralibus, judicialibus et cæremonialibus, tractat S. Thomas peroptime in prima secundæ.
paras.en: [[4:4|Remember the law of Moses my servant|Mementote legis Moysis servi mei]]: that is, since so fearful a judgment of God is to come, remember now without ceasing, and keep, the law of God given through Moses; [[4:4|which I commanded him in|quam mandavi ei in]] mount [[4:4|Horeb|Horeb]], that is, Sinai, where the written law was given to Moses, and the two tables of the testimony written by the finger of God; [[4:4|for all Israel|ad omnem Israel]], that is, that he should set it before all the children of Israel to be observed; [[4:4|the precepts|præcepta]], that is, those ten moral precepts, namely the Decalogue of the law, which are commanded to be kept in the New Testament too, Christ saying: [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si vis ad vitam intrare, serva mandata]]; [[4:4|and judgments|et judicia]], that is, the judicial precepts, which laid down the manner of living justly towards one's neighbour, as the ceremonial precepts of the law laid down the manner of conducting oneself towards the Creator in divine worship. The judicial precepts of the law, however, can be kept in the New Testament, if they are instituted anew by some Christian ruler fit for this: for they were not merely figurative. Of the threefold precepts of the law, namely the moral, the judicial and the ceremonial, St. Thomas treats excellently in the First Part of the Second Part [the Prima Secundae of his Summa Theologiae].

paras.t: Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam prophetam : qui simul cum Enoch vivit in paradiso terrestri, venietque cum eo instante Antichristi prædicatione. Hinc et Christus in Evangelio asserit : Elias quidem venturus est. Antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis, id est dies judicii : qui magnus terribilisque vocatur propter magna et terribilia opera Dei quæ fient in eo.
paras.en: [[4:5|Behold, I will send you Elias the prophet|Ecce ego mittam vobis Eliam prophetam]]: who lives together with Enoch in the earthly paradise, and will come with him at the time of Antichrist's preaching. Hence Christ too declares in the Gospel: [[Matt 17:11|Elias indeed shall come|Elias quidem venturus est]]. [[4:5|before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord|Antequam veniat dies Domini magnus et horribilis]], that is, the day of judgment: which is called great and dreadful because of the great and terrible works of God that will be done in it.

paras.t: Et convertet cor patrum ad filios, id est cor Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, aliorumque patrum antiquorum, ad Judæos, qui tunc credent in Christum, et cor filiorum ad patres eorum. Per hoc enim, quod Judæos tunc existentes convertet ad verum Christum, faciet inter eos et patres eorum plenam caritatis concordiam. Hoc idem angelus dixit de Joanne Baptista, ut scribit Lucas. Sicut enim Joannes prævenit primum Christi adventum, ita Elias secundum. Hinc in Ecclesiastico dicitur ad Eliam : Inscriptus es in judiciis temporum, lenire iracundiam Domini, conciliare cor patris ad filium, et restituere domus Jacob. Cui consonat quod in Evangelio ait Salvator : Elias quum venerit, restituet omnia. De Eliæ autem et Enoch prædicatione contra Antichristum, et occisione eorum ab ipso, multa in Apocalypsi leguntur.
paras.en: [[4:6|And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children|Et convertet cor patrum ad filios]], that is, the heart of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob and the other ancient fathers, to the Jews, who will then believe in Christ, [[4:6|and the heart of the children to their fathers|et cor filiorum ad patres eorum]]. For by converting the Jews then living to the true Christ, he will make a full concord of charity between them and their fathers. The angel said this same thing of John the Baptist, as Luke writes[[Luke 1:17||]]. For as John went before the first coming of Christ, so does Elias the second. Hence it is said to Elias in Ecclesiasticus: Thou [[Ecclus 48:10|art registered in the judgments of times to appease the wrath of the Lord, to reconcile the heart of the father to the son|Inscriptus es in judiciis temporum, lenire iracundiam Domini, conciliare cor patris ad filium]], and to restore the houses of Jacob [Denis reads domus, "houses", where the Vulgate has tribus, "tribes"]. With this agrees what the Saviour says in the Gospel: [[Mark 9:11|Elias, when he shall come|Elias quum venerit]], [[Mark 9:11|shall restore all things|restituet omnia]][[Matt 17:11||]]. Of the preaching of Elias and Enoch against Antichrist, and of their being slain by him, much is read in the Apocalypse[[Apoc 11:3||]].

paras.t: Ne forte veniam, et percutiam terram, id est terrenos atque incredulos, anathemate, id est omnimoda reprobatione ac separatione. Unde pro anathemate Septuaginta transtulerunt, Penitus. Quidam quoque affirmat, quod in Hebræo non habetur, Forte: de quo judicare non valeo; et tamen in translatione Septuaginta interpretum ponitur, Forte. Porro, sive sit in Hebræo, sive non, certum omnino est quod non ponitur tanquam dubitationis vel incertitudinis signum, sed ad insinuandum libertatem Judicis venientis.
paras.en: [[4:6|lest I come, and strike the earth|Ne forte veniam, et percutiam terram]], that is, the earthly-minded and unbelieving, [[4:6|with anathema|anathemate]], that is, with utter reprobation and separation. Hence for anathema the Septuagint translated: Utterly. Someone also affirms that Forte ["perhaps": the Vulgate reads ne forte, "lest perhaps", which the Douay-Rheims gives simply as "lest"] is not in the Hebrew: on which I am not able to judge; and yet in the translation of the Septuagint interpreters Forte is set down. But whether it is in the Hebrew or not, it is quite certain that it is not set down as a sign of doubt or uncertainty, but to suggest the freedom of the Judge who is coming.

4.title: De spirituali intelligentia capitulorum tertii et quarti.
4.title_en: On the spiritual understanding of the third and fourth chapters.
4.note: This article treats chapters 3 and 4 together; its commentary on chapter 3 is shown under that chapter.

paras.t: Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ. Hoc quotidie adimpletur. Dum enim peccator divinum attendens judicium, pœnitet, statim Christus eum illuminat, sicut Apostolus exhortatur : Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis, et illuminabit te Christus. Sed et proficientibus in caritate et gratia, Sol iste justitiæ omni hora splendidius micat, et clarius jubar infundit. Contemplativis vero et excellentius oritur, et radios theoriæ supernæ copiosius impertitur. Et sanitas, id est a peccati læsione immunitas, erit in pennis vestris : id est, pennæ hæ electorum in sæculo isto, quibus quotidie volant ad Deum, sunt oratio pura, meditatio sancta, contemplatio stabilita, et ceteri actus donorum atque virtutum : in quibus tunc sanitas oritur, dum vitiis non miscentur; imo si quid evagationis, venialisque culpæ se ingerat, caritatis fervore repente consumitur.
paras.en: [[4:2|But unto you that fear my name, the Sun of justice shall arise|Orietur vobis timentibus nomen meum Sol justitiæ]]. This is fulfilled daily. For when a sinner, heeding the divine judgment, repents, Christ at once enlightens him, as the Apostle exhorts: [[Eph 5:14|Rise, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead: and Christ shall enlighten thee|Surge, qui dormis, et exsurge a mortuis, et illuminabit te Christus]]. And to those too who are advancing in charity and grace this Sun of justice shines more brightly every hour, and pours in its radiance more clearly. To contemplatives, indeed, it rises still more excellently, and imparts more abundantly the rays of heavenly contemplation [theoria, the Greek word for contemplation]. [[4:2|and health|Et sanitas]], that is, freedom from the injury of sin, shall be in your [[4:2|wings|pennis]] [Denis reads in pennis vestris, "in your wings", where the Vulgate and the Douay-Rheims have "his wings"]: that is, these wings of the elect in this world, by which they fly daily to God, are pure prayer, holy meditation, settled contemplation and the other acts of the gifts and virtues: in which health then arises when they are not mixed with vices; nay, if any wandering or venial fault intrudes itself, it is at once consumed by the fervour of charity.

paras.t: Mementote legis Moysis servi mei. Multo amplius mente, ore, et facto memores esse debemus legis Christi unigeniti Filii Dei. Propter quod ad Hebræos scribit Apostolus : Irritam quis faciens legem Moysis, sine ulla miseratione duobus vel tribus testibus moritur : quanto magis putatis deteriora mereri supplicia, qui Filium Dei conculcaverit, et sanguinem testamenti pollutum duxerit, et spiritui gratiæ contumeliam fecerit?
paras.en: [[4:4|Remember the law of Moses my servant|Mementote legis Moysis servi mei]]. Much more ought we to be mindful, in mind, in word and in deed, of the law of Christ, the only-begotten Son of God. Wherefore the Apostle writes to the Hebrews: [[Heb 10:28|A man making void the law of Moses dieth without any mercy under two or three witnesses|Irritam quis faciens legem Moysis, sine ulla miseratione duobus vel tribus testibus moritur]]: [[Heb 10:29|How much more, do you think he deserveth worse punishments, who hath trodden under foot the Son of God|quanto magis putatis deteriora mereri supplicia, qui Filium Dei conculcaverit]], [[Heb 10:29|and hath esteemed the blood of the testament unclean|et sanguinem testamenti pollutum duxerit]], [[Heb 10:29|and hath offered an affront to the Spirit of grace?|et spiritui gratiæ contumeliam fecerit?]]

paras.t: Postremo, sicut Elias convertet sua prædicatione cor patrum ad filios, et econverso; sic omnis bonus prælatus, prædicator, pastor, seu doctor, qui alios ad viam æquitatis convertit, et corda eorum ad Deum reducit, convertit cor patrum, videlicet Apostolorum et aliorum Sanctorum, ad istos, et cor istorum ad illos, ut Deo simul cohæreant, atque in vinculo caritatis connexi permaneant. Similitudo quippe est causa amoris, et unit discordes, quemadmodum dissimilitudo separat copulatos. Hæc autem Christus per suos vicarios efficit, ne veniens imparatos condemnet. Multis etenim modis nos ad se revocare non cessat, qui vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad veritatis pervenire notitiam, qui est cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto super omnia Deus sublimis et benedictus. Amen.
paras.en: Lastly, as Elias by his preaching [[4:6|shall turn|convertet]] [[4:6|the heart of the fathers to the children|cor patrum ad filios]], and conversely; so every good prelate, preacher, pastor or doctor who turns others to the way of equity and brings their hearts back to God, turns the heart of the fathers, namely of the Apostles and the other Saints, to these, and the heart of these to them, that they may cleave together to God, and remain joined in the bond of charity. For likeness is the cause of love, and unites those at variance, as unlikeness separates those joined together. And Christ does this through His vicars, lest at His coming He condemn the unprepared. For in many ways He does not cease to call us back to Himself, [[1 Tim 2:4|Who will have all men to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth|qui vult omnes homines salvos fieri, et ad veritatis pervenire notitiam]], who with the Father and the Holy Ghost is God sublime and blessed above all. Amen.
